# Farrell Style Guide

Horror documentary style, learned from the 5 Farrell references. Rev 52, saved 2026-11-12T13:53:49.
Follow it top to bottom on every Farrell edit. The rule book comes first and is never skipped.

How to read it: *(set by you)* marks the channel owner's own rules; the rest are learned from the references. Both are binding. "see vNN · title" names an example clip on the Farrell board (v01 Internet Archive, v02 YouTube Kids, v03 TV news, v04 Russian internet, v05 Arabic internet). A *treated* (graphic) shot is anything built in the edit: pages, photos, titles, maps. *Raw footage* is source video kept as it is; it gets no added texture, vignette or desaturation.

## Rule book (never break these)

1. Mood is horror, always. Every picture, text, movement and sound adds dread or unease. Nothing bright, cute or playful unless it is glitched, desaturated or distorted so it feels wrong. One exception: the white flash transition (rule 3).
2. All text you add uses the VCR OSD Mono font: dates, labels, captions, comment cards. No second font. One exception: the case title card copies the project's card design (small gold VCR 'CASE N' over a big white condensed title). Captured pages, posts and broadcasts keep their own fonts.
3. Between shots, cut straight or use one of these transitions: crossfade, dip to black, VHS (any approved variant from the VHS set, with its SFX), glitch, white flash or split-screen wipe. Most transitions are crossfades (about 1.2 s) and dips to black. Use VHS and the white flash (flashbang) only rarely, for example to show an article or page. No other wipes, slides, spins, zoom transitions or shape reveals. One device exception: WarpCard enters on its own warp slide-in.
4. Shot size is mostly medium. Use close-up or extreme close-up only to point at a detail (a face, a word, a figure in the frame).
5. Compose to the centre: the subject, title or key line sits on the centre of the frame. Exception: camcorder OSD and CCTV HUD text sits in the corners, because it is part of the device look; the subject still sits centre. The camcorder clock may tick its seconds.
6. High contrast, dark grade, vintage texture. Treated shots sit at a median brightness of 70-90 on a 0-255 scale. Before the first edit, pick 3-5 texture types for the video (film grain, VHS noise and tracking lines, CRT scanlines and curvature, dust and scratches, light leak), list them in the edit notes, and put at least one on every treated shot.
7. Every graphic shot moves: pan, zoom or push, tracking, 3D tilt, or wide angle, sometimes with lens distortion. No still graphics. Keep lens distortion very light and fixed: it is already there from the first frame and never animates; a slight bulge and faint colour fringes; text stays straight and easy to read.
8. Raw clip audio: start the audio 1.0 s before its picture cut (pre-roll; less if the source has no 1.0 s of head) and end it with the picture. Fade in over the first 3.22 s and out over the last 2.74 s. If the audio clip is shorter than 5.96 s, multiply both fade lengths by (clip length / 5.96) x 0.98.
9. Crossfade inside a montage and between most shots. Dip to black between sections (a new date, place or time period). A dip to black is a must at the end of a case, into its title card, and again at the end of the title card. VHS and the white flash are rare: an article, a page, or a rare shock reveal.
10. **Narration and raw clips only**: No real person on camera as host or presenter. Every video is narration over raw clips; chapter turns use title cards and the narration, never a cut back to a host.
11. **Follow the cut sheet**: Follow the cut sheet. For each narration beat, its VISUAL, SOURCE and EDIT NOTES decide the picture and the moment each comment or graphic comes in. Do not add a graphic that the cut sheet or the spoken words do not ask for.
12. **Real footage first**: Real footage first. Graphics support the footage; they never fill the time. Put comment cards over real footage from the case (as the PROJECT edit does), not on plain black. Show one comment, then go back to the video. Most of the running time is real footage.
13. **Comments on the real page**: Show comments as real screenshots of the real YouTube comments when you can. Crop to the comment that matters (do not show the whole section) and highlight only that main comment. The screenshot floats in: it slides up from the bottom of the frame with easing, or it comes in with a slow 3D pan; vary them. If the real comment cannot be found, make your own comment card. When a reply follows its parent, the card grows to fit (shape morph) with easing and the reply crossfades in. No hard cut inside one thread.
14. **Smooth easing, nothing pops**: Every animation flows: eased in and out (for example ease-in-out cubic), with no snap, no jump and no cut in the middle. Every card enters and exits with an eased fade and scale; it never vanishes in one frame. If an animation is jerky, fix its easing; do not remove it. Every card stays fully on screen and centred, with a safe margin, on every frame.
15. **No still shots**: No still shots. Every shot longer than about 2 s moves: a slow push (2-5 %/s) or a slow drift. This includes raw footage and photos (add motion only). Raw footage keeps its own colour: no Nocturn grade, no Lumetri look, no added vignette or desaturation; the video-wide texture layer goes on top of everything and is the only thing added (owner, 2026-11-10; overrides the old 'grade raws toward Nocturn' lesson).
16. **Show the thing named**: When the narration names an animal, object or thing the viewer may not know (for example a raccoon or a tanuki), show a real photo of it with a slow push. Use a free-licence photo (for example Wikimedia Commons) and keep its source and licence in the edit notes.
17. **Captions match the audio**: Raw captions match the raw audio. Each caption starts within 2 frames of its spoken line and ends when the line ends (hold it a little longer only to reach the minimum). The text says what is said. Each caption stays on screen at least 5/6 s and at most 7 s; a line too short for 5/6 s is joined with the next line. Never hold a caption over silence. Exception: a caption that translates text shown on screen stays while that text shows. Check every caption against the audio.
18. **Feedback loop**: Every owner note on a render goes into this guide the same day (rule book entry or rule, plus a Learnings entry, via model.apply_ops + model.save). The next build must read the rule book, the open Learnings and styleguide/_shared/GENERIC_RULES.md first; after each render check it against every line, fix what fails, then deliver.
19. **No ultra-short shots**: No ultra-short shots. A narration shot (B-roll, photo or graphic under the narration) is on screen alone, outside its transitions, for at least 3 s. Raw clips keep the length the cut sheet gives. If a beat is too short, extend a neighbouring shot or merge the beat; never squeeze in a quick extra shot.
20. **Clean crossfades**: Clean crossfades: during a crossfade or dip, both clips play continuous footage. No source cut (a change of camera shot inside the source) may fall inside the transition or its handles, not even a soft cut between similar shots. A dip to black is an even eased curve: the old clip fades down smoothly over half the dip, the new clip fades up over the other half (never a fast drop to black in a few frames). Overlays (stamps, captions) on a shot appear and go only while the shot plays alone, never during its fades. After each render, check every transition frame by frame in the final file: no frame-difference spike inside a fade.
21. **Blur behind comments and title cards**: When a comment (card or page screenshot) or a title card is on screen, the footage behind it keeps playing, blurred and darkened, so the comment or title is the sharpest and brightest thing in the frame.
22. **Nothing still for too long**: Nothing sits still for too long. A non-raw shot where nothing happens is changed within about 4-5 s (new footage, new angle or a comment). Long held shots are allowed only for raw clips the cut sheet asks for.
23. **Comments stay long enough to read**: A comment stays on screen long enough to read it: at least 3.5 s in total, entry and exit included, and the full time the narration talks about it. Aim for reading time: characters / 15 + 1 s (the narration reading it aloud may cover the rest). If the narration does not give a comment 3.5 s, leave the comment out; never flash a comment in and out. A comment's slide, pan, lift or grow motion never runs during a crossfade or dip of the footage behind it (the comment may stay still on screen across a fade).
24. **Rule check before render**: Before every render, run the rule check on the edit list (scratchpad kit: rulecheck.py <edl>). It must pass with no FAIL: narration shots 3 s alone, shots 2.5 s total, captions 5/6-7 s, comments 3.5 s, no overlay motion inside a fade. Before picking a source in-point, scan the source for camera cuts (srcscan.py) so no cut falls in a fade. After render, check every fade in the final file (fadescan.py).
25. **Overlay and its footage are one shot**: A motion graphic (comment, card) and the blurred footage behind it are one shot. The short-shot rules count it that way: plain footage between two overlays, or between an overlay and a shot change, is either 0 s or at least 3 s alone. Two comments in a row: the next one slides up while the old one leaves, and the blur stays on (no sharp footage flashes between them). A comment that is still on screen when its footage crossfades to a new shot fades out with that shot during the crossfade (opacity follows the fade, no lift); it never leaves just before the fade. Same at entry: a comment can fade in with its shot. A reply thread shows the full thread (parent + reply) from its first frame, with the reply's translation already under it; no grow/morph step, because viewers do not need to read the parent alone.
26. **Easing palette**: Easing palette. Default: ease-in-out cubic (power2.inOut), about 1.0 s, for most moves. Cards, labels and titles that land: ease-out quart (power3.out), about 1.1 s. One big reveal per section: ease-out expo (expo.out), about 1.5 s. Slow drifts, pans and glints: ease-in-out sine (sine.inOut), about 1.5 s or longer. Never bounce, elastic or back easing.
27. **Approved Motion Lab moves**: The 34 Motion Lab moves approved on 2026-11-10 are in Motion graphics (source user). Vary them: do not use the same comment, title or label move twice in a row. New approved devices: colour-split title settle, camcorder OSD and CCTV HUD corner text, redaction reveal, case dossier, archive terminal, VHS tape label, Please stand by card and 2.5D parallax collage. Line and path draws are trim paths: the line grows from start to end with an ease-in-out curve and a glowing tip, and the next point pops when the tip lands. The CRT scan reveal for comments was rejected on 2026-11-10. A marker or pulse ring shows only after the trim path has fully reached its point, never before. A TV switch-off goes: picture flares, squeezes to a bright line, the line shrinks to a glowing dot, the dot fades. A push-in that ends with a screen or page filling the frame has no end transition: hold on the full frame, no fade, no dip.
28. **Graphics look real**: Motion graphics are built from real material: footage stills, page screenshots, real-looking players, comments, documents and maps. Do not add film grain, scratches or VHS texture to a graphic. That texture goes once, on the video track, over everything.
29. **Every case gets a map**: Every case gets a map on its place line, even when the clause is under 8 s. The map holds on into the next clause so its animation can finish; it never flashes past. This overrides the old 'map only when the clause is about 8 s or more' lesson.
30. **Bleep unbleeped profanity**: Profanity in raw audio is MUTED: the raw audio goes silent over the word only, with no bleep tone, and its caption shows "[ __ ]" in place of the word. Check every raw clip's transcript for profanity before the storyboard is approved and list each mute with its source time.
31. Under narration, raw clip audio is fully muted (no bed at all). Raw audio plays only in raw moments with no narration over them; short fade-in and fade-out at their edges are fine.
32. Intro case carousel: when the narration says there are N encounters, show N case cards (portrait cards with a looping clip of each case) sliding sideways in one continuous move with easing, never pausing. The centre card is larger and bright, the side cards are smaller and darker. Background: dark with an icy blue fog glow behind the cards (never red). The last card slides to centre and zooms with easing until it fills the screen, landing on the first frame of the next clip. Reference: Pinterest pin 970525788470144809 (Netflix-style carousel).
33. Every case shows the source creator's YouTube channel page as a 3D tilt-and-pan zoom. All website / page 3D shots are centred in frame and slightly zoomed in, never drifting to one side.
34. **One caption look**: All captions use one look across the whole video: white VCR OSD Mono text on a black box. No other caption colours. Captions are in sentence case (never all caps). (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
35. Owner changes are made per section: re-render only the changed section(s) and splice them into the full video. Never re-render the whole video for a local change.
36. **Caption every mute**: Every muted curse word gets a "[ __ ]" caption at the mute, even in raw clips that otherwise have no captions. The token "[ __ ]" is one unit and never wraps across lines (keep it on one line; write it with non-breaking spaces). (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
37. **Captions on every raw**: Every raw clip with speech inside the cases gets captions (all spoken words, not only key lines). The intro (cold open, carousel, title) gets no raw captions. Where the creator's own subtitles are burned in, keep theirs and add none on top. Creator burned-in text can be larger than briefed and moves when the raw is zoomed (teaser copies): measure its box on a still for each use and raise our caption bottom only on that raw (van used y 855 / 840). (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
38. Caption width: one caption line is at most about 55% of the frame width (about 1050 px at 1080p). Longer text wraps to a second line, then a third line (max 3 lines), centred, white VCR OSD Mono on a black box.
39. When the source gives no location, do NOT show a 'LOCATION UNDISCLOSED' graphic. Show a clip from the source of the person travelling to or arriving at the place (drive, hike in, walking to camp) for the same time, to keep the pacing.
40. **Stamp ends early**: A date/place stamp ends before its shot ends (at least 0.2 s), never over the next shot or its caption. (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
41. **Crops exclude overlays**: ENHANCED / zoom / slow-replay crops must exclude creator overlays (arrows, logos, burned text): check a still of the whole crop span; move the crop or the in point if any edge shows one. (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
42. **Opener follows VO**: Case-opening graphics follow the VO word order: map when the place is said, article when the article is named, channel page when the channel is named. Check each graphic's in point against the VO word timing. (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
43. **Non-English source captions**: Non-English sources: caption from the channel's own English subtitles (yt-dlp). Whisper misdetects rare languages; fallback = the cut sheet's English lines timed on the speech spans. (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
44. **Glyphs need a font**: Comment or card text in a non-Latin script needs a font that has those glyphs (VCR OSD Mono has no Cyrillic: it showed empty boxes). Check a still of every non-Latin card. (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
45. **Missing comment fallback**: A cut-sheet comment not found in the fetched comments: use a real fetched comment, or recreate it from the cut-sheet text with no handle. List every recreated or substituted comment for the owner to check. (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
46. **Independent visual QC**: Every section gets an independent visual QC (a separate agent, still sheets of every graphic, caption, box and crop) before the music pass. In van it caught defects the builders missed in 3 of 12 sections. (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
47. **Versions after music**: The music pass writes the next version (caseN_vK+1). A picture fix after music = a new higher version, then rerun music on it. The full build takes the newest caseN_vK of each case. (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
48. **One writer per file**: Production: one writer per output file (two writers corrupted the winter full build); never two final renders of one case at once; max 2 NVENC encodes per agent; check free disk first (a full build needs about the sum of the section sizes). (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
49. **Open: graphics lag 0.6 s**: OPEN ISSUE for the next video: picture and graphics land about 0.6 s after the EDL time (measured case 9; suspect the first shot's in-handle kept in assembly). Measure on the first section and fix before relying on EDL times. (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
50. **Music per video, limiter**: Music: use different Epidemic Sound tracks for each video (never reuse the last video's beds). Master: retry the limiter with the ceiling 1 dB lower until true peak <= -1.05 dBTP (AAC overshoot failed at -0.97). (van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11)
51. Owner 2026-11-11: Winter and Van full videos were not up to the mark. Follow the Nocturn channel style (youtube.com/@Nocturn_real). Where Nocturn and older Farrell rules clash, Nocturn wins; timing and caption-timing rules stay.
52. Intro motion graphic is different on every video. Never reuse an earlier video's intro graphic.
53. Motion graphics all through the video, not only at case starts: date cards, location/date stamps, source-page captures with red highlight bars on the key line, picture-in-picture second angle, zooms to details.
54. Music under the whole video, no dry gaps. SFX on every cut, card, highlight and scare. Master near -13 LUFS integrated (Nocturn measured -11.5 to -17.5, most -13).
55. Nocturn grade on footage only (never on captions, cards or page captures): lifted blacks, warm-red mids, slight blue lift in shadows, saturation 1.12, soft vignette. ffmpeg chain in productions/_nocturn-ref/grade/nocturn_grade.txt. Target footage YAVG about 75-88, SATAVG about 8-11.
56. Nocturn cold open: scariest raw moment first with small VCR captions, then a VHS date card (e.g. JULY 2022) on grey/black, then the story.
57. Nocturn intros: every one differs; no logo or title card first. Order: scariest raw or vlog, then page capture, then date card at 45-80 s. Intro mix 1-3 dB louder than the rest.
58. Date card variants: grey VCR-mono card; bold sans on dark vignette with place in smaller type below; or date text straight over the clip. Dip to black before a card.
59. Extra Nocturn graphics: channel popup pill (avatar+name, 2-3 s); boxed mono name tag on a person; red arrow + red uppercase label; red redaction bars; tilted page capture over blurred bg; glowing time-jump title ('2 YEARS EARLIER...'); news lower third; numbered red-frame preview grid that zooms into item 1.
60. Transitions: about 85-90% hard cuts; short dissolves next; RGB-split glitch every 20-60 s; flashes rare.
61. Censor: Gaussian blur or pixel mosaic. Captions on raw speech always, one line 3-7 words; narration not captioned.
62. Pacing: intro shots ~8 s median, body ~14 s; graphics 2-4 s each; raw clips 10-60 s. Designed SFX hits ~4-10 per minute (est.). Music/ambience never fully silent; master ~-13 LUFS.
63. Footage share: keep raw footage as the base. Across 15 Nocturn videos raw is 42-92% of runtime, median 72%, graphics median 28%. Add a graphic only to prove, date, locate or point at something the narration names. Do not cover a raw run of 10-60 s with a graphic that adds no fact.
64. Case open: dip to black (0.3-1.5 s), then a date card or date title within 3-5 s, then the source page or a map, then raw footage. Seen in 13 of 15 videos with a dated start. Optional: 5-30 s of the next case's raw footage under the closing line before the dip (5 of 15).
65. Case close: no outro card. End on the last proof image (comments page or article with a red bar, 10 of 15) or on the last raw footage with the outcome in narration (7 of 15). Then a dip to black, about 1 s (13 of 15). Use a quiet photo with a colour drain for a death or loss (3 of 15). End the video on a fade to black.
66. Source proof: show the source on screen. Put the real YouTube watch page, with the footage playing inside, at the start of a case (8 of 15), then expand to full frame. Add a channel pop-up (2-3 s) or channel page when naming the creator. Show comments on a dark page, 6-12 s (11 of 15). Show every page 3-10 s.
67. Highlight and callout: on every article, post or comment page, sweep a red, yellow or blue bar over the one line the voice reads (12 of 15). On footage, point at the detail with a red circle, box, arrow or typed label for 1-10 s, not a cutaway (6 of 15). Repeat the same label when that footage returns.
68. Name tags and dates: when a person is named, show a small serif or mono name tag on them for 1-4 s, or a framed portrait over a blurred dark copy of the face (9 of 15). Date cards: small white text, 2-6 s, fade up from black or over dim footage; type it word by word with a red last word if you want emphasis (13 of 15).
69. Glitch and transitions: dissolve pages in and out over 10-16 frames; never hard cut to a page (12 of 15). Use an RGB tear of 8-13 frames, or a static burst of 0.1-1 s, at graphic edges and scares (12 of 15). Do not use it on every cut. Use no wipes between cases; use the black dip.
70. Layouts and diagrams: for a list, show a numbered grid of 6-10 red-framed clips, 4-8 s, with shrink, pan and zoom into item 1; reuse it as a recap (4 of 15). For a plan, deal or timeline, build a hand-drawn board where stills, handwriting and arrows appear one by one, 5-33 s (3 of 15). Use red node lines for links between people.
71. Graphic pacing: a graphic lasts 2-10 s, mean about 8 s; a page or comments break comes every 30-60 s inside a long raw run. Headline flashes on a spoken list run 0.7-1.2 s each. Maps run 3-15 s. Keep a cold open: strongest raw footage first, no logo or title at 0:00 (11 of 15 start on raw).
72. No wind bed. Under raw clips and the cold open use the music or a low ambient drone instead.
73. Level order, always: narration loudest, music clearly under it (about 13 dB), SFX under the music. SFX must never break the flow or mask narration or music.
74. Booms and risers may sit a little higher than other SFX (about 3 dB under the music). Glitch, static, VHS, creak and other high or harsh SFX sit much lower (about 9-12 dB under the music); low-pass harsh high-pitch SFX.
75. To mark an object (e.g. the buried tent): keep the object in full colour and slightly fade and desaturate the rest of the frame, or draw a clean red circle. Never a random polygon outline.
76. Map animations must look finished and smooth (Nocturn-style 3D/aerial tilt, clean labels), not a flat tile pan.
77. **Generic rules**: Follow styleguide/_shared/GENERIC_RULES.md (shot length >= 3 s, audio cutting, SFX/music levels, loudness, transition hygiene, smoothness, QC, feedback loop). This guide's own rule book wins only where it says so explicitly.

## 1. Overall aesthetic

A dark, archival internet-horror documentary. Most of the running time is web pages, comments and photos laid out as tilted 3D sheets on a dark ground, cut against long stretches of raw source footage. Graphics are desaturated and grainy; raw footage keeps its own colour and age. In the 5 references, motion graphics make up 45-80% of the clips.

- Show evidence as the thing itself: the real web page, comment, file name or broadcast, in 3D on a dark ground, never a re-typed version. — see v01 · Subreddit listing, dark, 3D tilt; v04 · 'Russian Slenderman' blog, translated; v02 · CCTV figure watch page
- Alternate treated graphics with long runs of untouched raw footage; raw footage keeps its own colour and period look. — see v03 · Gunman on air; v01 · Raw footage: leaked full video (glitching)
- High contrast and vintage texture on every treated shot (rule 6). *(set by you)* — see v01 · Website 'THE TIME IS UP', push in; v04 · Screenshots, red circles
- **Motion graphics use**: "Do both": a spatial idea can take B-roll and the explaining graphic.
- **Motion graphics use**: Open a case on the channel page in a 3D pan when the first clause names the channel; the plate ends on the next noun, 4-8 s.
- **Motion graphics use**: Never use a stand-in for an unsourceable place or document; change the plan and say which beat changed.
- **Motion graphics use**: Never show another YouTube channel's page unless the narration names it; replace foreign-language documents and AI stills with real material.
- **Motion graphics use**: Nothing on a plate may flicker or boil; texture lives in geometry, not a filter; map dashes and labels must not crawl or snap.
- **Motion graphics use**: Not too much animation: labels ease in and stay put, no springy bounce, one ease over a whole move (no stop at each keyframe).
- **Motion graphics use**: An arrow tip lands short of the subject; the ring is parented to the shot; do not mark what the viewer cannot see.
- **Motion graphics use**: Look at a plate at 3-4x reduction; marks must survive small.
- **Motion graphics use**: A card push can clip its own text; keep push at or under 0.8 %/s or pad the page; check the last frame.
- **Motion graphics use**: A graphic used more than once in a case is one component with a state; only the annotation layer changes.
- **Motion graphics use**: Archive photos get a gentler camera than screenshots; a plate whose own printed caption names the place is worth reframing for.
- **Motion graphics use**: A map dive opens already framing the place, then pushes in slowly; never open wide or zoom-bounce.
- **Motion graphics use**: A quote the viewer already heard lands whole (not typed on); only the words that carry the story light up.
- **Motion graphics use**: A single figure lands whole and its unit follows; never type a number on; only a real countdown gets the alarm colour.
- **Motion graphics use**: When there is no document (declared fiction), illustrate with a drawing that claims nothing.
- **Motion graphics use**: Pick the projection that shows the relation (plan, section, elevation); context marks go down light, the carrying mark pressed hard.
- **Motion graphics use**: Study how each reference opens a case; one opening animation plus one odd device is not enough.
- **Motion graphics use**: Give each case its own house style and opener; do not copy one case's devices into all of them, reuse only small utilities.
- **Motion graphics use**: Maps use satellite plates only (no OSM patchwork), never zoomed past native resolution, and open already zoomed in near the place with the place highlighted from the start.
- **Motion graphics use**: Explainers (line-art, neon pictograms) only where the narration explains a mechanism, laid over dimmed blurred case footage and never on black.
- **Motion graphics use**: Look-here marks (rings, freezes, punches) are silent, and at most about 3 freeze-punches per video.
- **Motion graphics use**: Red is never used on red or warm plates (white text, contrast 4.5:1 or better).
- **Motion graphics use**: Pages enter in varied ways (cut, short flash, flash-streak, one white frame, fade, glitch) and the treatment rotates between full, card over blurred clip and tilted handheld.
- **QC check**: Verify by looking: a frame at the midpoint of each new shot, tiled; verify the cut as well as the picks.
- **QC check**: Measure first, sheet second, watch last; a contact sheet proves a device exists, not that it is absent.
- **QC check**: A number from one reference is that video's quirk; use three or more same-format references and treat a range as a sanity check.
- **QC check**: Read the reference itself before building to it; a summary is not the study.
- **QC check**: A detector count is a floor; calibrate thresholds on the footage (black is the file floor + 6, not luma 10).
- **QC check**: Run a freeze audit on every used source range; sources can freeze by themselves.
- **QC check**: Gap checks must catch below one frame (0.005 s) so 1-frame black flashes are found.
- **QC check**: Settle motion claims with flow numbers: max frame-to-frame velocity change under about 0.7 px, no zero-velocity dips.
- **QC check**: Report which beat was changed and why, mark shots confirmed/generic/absent, and say what stays unverified.
- **QC check**: QC every case: black frames, freezes, silences, loudness, no creator speech under narration, and a frame sheet of the finished case.
- **QC check**: Never claim something is done or verified unless it is.
- **QC check**: Frame tolerance is plus or minus 1 frame; black check threshold 0.005 s; undecodable files and missing audio are critical, unplanned black and bad frames are repairable.
- **QC check**: Freeze of 2 s or more and silence of 1 s or more below -60 dB are flagged for human review; a narration range 90% silent counts as missing narration.
- **QC check**: Warn when an audio join jumps more than 18 dB, a source peaks at 0 dBFS, or the delivery pixel format is not yuv420p.
- **Motion graphics use**: For the police/CCTV series use the red circle, block arrow and red title measured from the reference, not hand-drawn h-paper.
- **Motion graphics use**: Highlight blend follows the page: screen on dark pages, multiply on light pages.
- **Motion graphics use**: Place a red reveal ring only in the calmest camera window: sweep inter-frame difference over the source, and difference two frames seconds apart to catch slow events.
- **Motion graphics use**: Overlay graphics go on a separate track with a transparent background.
- **QC check**: Scan the whole source for burned-in title cards and letterboxed outros before choosing any fill range.
- **QC check**: Measure the clean picture region of an inset CCTV news package per region before punching in.
- **QC check**: True black is the clip's own floor plus about 4 (floor 16 on limited range); a mean<12-15 test wrongly condemns dark night footage.
- **QC check**: Measure luma on every fill frame; a contact sheet does not catch a shot that plays as black.
- **QC check**: Verify scratch audio tracks by clip count; a stray unmuted clip hid under the narration despite a blanket 'all 0' claim.
- **QC check**: Check each source folder holds the right video: the download order was not the case order (7 of 8 folders held the wrong video).

## 2. Mood and emotion

Horror, built from restraint rather than shocks: dark pages that drift, a calm narrator, and moments where the narration stops so the real footage or audio plays on its own. Dread comes from the evidence being real and the viewer being made to look closely at it.

- Build dread slowly: a dark page that drifts or pushes in while the narration states the unsettling fact plainly. — see v01 · Website 'THE TIME IS UP', push in; v01 · Dark Reddit comment thread, slow drift
- At the key moment, stop explaining: hold on the real footage with no graphics or text over it (sound: see Music & sound). — see v05 · Witch video ending, source audio; v05 · Abdullah footage: doors and noises
- Re-create events nobody filmed with dark silhouettes, never with actors' faces. — see v03 · Silhouette re-enactment: party; v03 · Silhouette re-enactment: party
- Keep one channel style for every video; "something of your own" means better templates inside the style, never a new look.
- Smoothness is a must: every move eased, every hand-over planned (J-cuts, cut on motion, no jumpy points, no repeated or frozen frames, graphics oversize then settle).
- Fix everything, not only what the owner named; gate each case side by side against the references before he sees it.
- Age-restriction rule: hook and title tiles never show a person struck, hurt or in danger, even blurred; show the event, end on the strongest non-human peak; cut before contact inside cases.
- Blur injured or dead faces in every frame (including before the incident); never tint or ring people red.
- Licensing: no clips whose rights sit with agencies (Jukin, ViralHog, Storyful, Newsflare); no station-shot TV b-roll.
- Thumbnails show no visible person, use a bodycam perspective, and keep the threat as an unseen or ghostly figure.

## 3. Color palette

Near-black grounds, desaturated pages and two accent colours. Treated shots measure 14-19% saturation against 20-42% for raw footage, with a neutral tint. Gold marks names, dates and titles; red marks warnings and circles on evidence; green and red/blue splits appear only in glitches.

- Desaturate graphics to 15-20% saturation; leave raw footage at its own colour. — see v01 · YouTube comments, vignette, scroll; v04 · 'Russian Slenderman' blog, translated
- Use gold for names, years and titles over a blurred background. — see v01 · Gold year title '1996' over blur; v01 · Dip to black, gold date '2005/07/02'
- Use red only to warn or to point: a red chapter word or a red circle on the figure. — see v03 · Red '1991' title; v05 · Zoomed frame, red circle on figure; v04 · Screenshots, red circles
- Keep green and red/blue split colour for glitch moments only. One exception: the colour-split title settle (red and blue copies slide into one clean white title, about 1.3 s), at most once per video. — see v01 · Wayback home + green matrix overlay; v01 · Comments on green with red/blue bars + glitch
- Grade to measured targets pooled over every used range, never one frame; a landed grade is never carried to another case as a preset.
- Night footage gets a smaller lift; one global grade turns night into grey haze; lift per range, not per case or series.
- Leave saturation high enough that a mono echo keeps its meaning.
- Measure every placed frame's mean luma; swap a near-black shot rather than rescuing it in the grade.
- Fill and grade only as much as asked; propose the rest rather than doing it.
- Measure darkness inside the picture area on vertical or pillarboxed footage, not the full frame.
- Night footage is lifted until it reads; look is muted colour with reds kept, deep contrast, soft bloom, vignette and grain.
- Never stack creative LUTs: at most one LUT per shot, blended by intensity; a missing LUT stops the plan and is never substituted.
- Warrior Mind LUT pick by pooled brightness: above 65 daylight, 28-65 main night warm, below 28 dark-footage lift; the near-black evidence LUT is chosen by hand only.
- A shot with mean luma under about 8 (8-bit) counts as near-black and is swapped, not graded.
- Fix dark night raw by lifting (exposure +1.9, shadows +45, blacks +5, contrast +10); blacks -10 crushes it and blacks +20 turns grey.
- Treat measured look figures as targets, not directions, and pool every used source range before grading because one frame can invert the answer.
- Grade after the cut is locked, in order exposure, white balance, contrast, saturation, creative look; match shots before making any look good.
- Use a blurred enlarged fill behind a pillarboxed or letterboxed clip, with a frame-count guard.

## 4. Lighting

Lighting is built in the edit: dark grounds, a vignette on almost every graphic and pools of light on the subject. In the references the edges of treated shots are 10-34% darker than the centre, and about 1 in 5 treated frames is near-black (brightness under 40 of 255).

- Put a vignette on every graphic so the edges fall 10-35% darker than the centre. — see v01 · YouTube comments, vignette, scroll; v01 · Stock photo with vignette
- Pages and photos sit on near-black, never on white or a bright colour. — see v01 · Dark Reddit comment thread, slow drift; v01 · Archived URLs isolated on black
- Darken and blur the page behind any title or overlay so the text is the brightest thing on screen. — see v01 · Gold title 'THE INTERNET ARCHIVE' over blur; v01 · 'necrobabes.org' gold title over blurred page

## 5. Camera angles

Mostly medium framing: a page section, a comment, a person from the chest up. Close-ups and extreme close-ups are saved for a detail the narration names, usually reached by zooming in on the same image. Pages are shown at an angle (3D tilt) rather than flat on.

- Medium shot by default (rule 4): enough of the page or person to read the context. *(set by you)* — see v01 · Host on camera; v01 · Tour listing page, tilt down
- Reach a close-up by zooming into the same image, on the detail the narration names (rule 4). *(set by you)* — see v05 · Zoomed frame, red circle on figure; v01 · Google Maps route, then zoom on pin
- Show pages and posts at a 3D angle, tilted away from the viewer, not flat on. — see v01 · Airport website, tilt and scroll down; v01 · Reddit post r/InternetMysteries, 3D tilt + drift

## 6. Camera movement

Every graphic moves (rule 7). Push-ins dominate: in a 60 s sample, 64% of all shots moved (raw footage included) and 77% of the moves were zoom-ins. Add pans across pages, tilts and slow drifts, tracking along maps and Street View, and the occasional wide-angle or distorted move.

- Push in slowly on the page as the narration gets to the point. — see v01 · Fifth Nail blog homepage, 3D zoom in; v01 · Website 'THE TIME IS UP', push in
- Pan or tilt across long pages and newspaper clippings to read them. *(set by you)* — see v01 · Tilted Twitter profile, pan; v01 · Newspaper clipping, pan
- Track along maps, satellite views and Street View to place the story. *(set by you)* — see v04 · Satellite pan to the road; v04 · Street View drive
- Use a 3D tilt with a slow drift for comment threads and posts; sometimes a wide-angle or distorted move for unease. *(set by you)* — see v01 · Reddit post r/InternetMysteries, 3D tilt + drift; v01 · Dark Reddit comment thread, slow drift

## 7. Shot composition

Centred and layered: a blurred, darkened copy of the page fills the frame, and the item that matters (a title, comment, file name or photo) sits in the middle on top. Old TV footage is placed inside a CRT frame or composited into rooms instead of being stretched.

- Centre the subject (rule 5): titles, labels and key comments sit in the middle of the frame. *(set by you)* — see v01 · Gold title 'THE INTERNET ARCHIVE' over blur; v05 · Title 'ARAB GHOST HUNTING'
- Layer: blurred page behind, the item that matters on top in the centre. — see v01 · 'necrobabes.org' gold title over blurred page; v01 · Game box art over blur, then gameplay
- Isolate a single line, URL or reply on black and highlight the word that matters. — see v01 · Archived URLs isolated on black; v01 · German forum reply on black, highlight on name
- Place old TV and video inside a CRT or screen frame rather than stretching it to fill. — see v05 · Western ghost-hunt shows in CRT frame; v02 · Screens comped into rooms

## 8. Editing rhythm

A block is a run of shots with one look (for example, all tilted-page shots), ending when the look changes. Expect 4-6 blocks per minute. Graphic blocks run 8-11 s; raw-footage blocks run 11-16 s and up to 27 s; title cards 2-4 s. Inside a block the picture keeps changing, so the cut still feels quick (the 60 s sample averaged 1.4 s per shot).

- Hold graphic blocks 8-11 s and raw-footage blocks 11-16 s; let a raw moment run to 25 s or more when it is the evidence. — see v03 · Gunman on air; v01 · Raw news footage + narration
- Keep title and date cards to 2-4 s. — see v03 · HOOLIGANISM title; v01 · Gold year title '1996' over blur
- Change the picture inside a block (a new page, photo or push) every 1-3 s while narration runs. — see v04 · Screenshots, red circles; v01 · Still photos: Brandes portrait, bathroom, cough syrup
- Never run narration over empty black: if the ground is black, something sits on it (text, a page, a photo). — see v01 · Source end text on black
- Read the narration, then look at the footage, before choosing any shot.
- One scene, one clip: length is not the rule, one image per clip is; do not cut a continuous scene into many same-picture cuts.
- Dense, eventful narration wants tight cuts; long exposition with nothing to show gets fewer, longer holds, never cuts for no informational reason.
- Cut on the clause (midpoint of the pause), not by feel, and never shorter than about 2 s; shot length is an output of the narration.
- When a proper noun sits inside a clause, the picture arrives exactly on that noun.
- The picture must be the literal subject of its clause (right time of day, right register), one picture per list item.
- Search for the action the narration describes, not its noun; if a line cannot be shown, cover the destination, never a stand-in actor.
- A different time range of the same scene is not a different picture; vary the framing.
- Check head, middle and tail of a picked range; a pick that works at 4 s can straddle a cut at 8 s.
- Dark is not black: a dark but readable range can be the best material; lift it to judge it before discarding.
- A freeze is a choice, not a mechanism: repeat the moving footage instead of freezing, freeze only for an examination beat the narration names.
- A reveal mark (ring/box) needs a still camera; choose the calmest window.
- Fill from the case's own source between neighbouring evidence beats; stock last; raw footage 70%+ under narration.
- Derive the fill strategy from what the source is; a single-framing source is monotonous, so do not manufacture cuts to hide it.
- A still image inside a footage video stays short (a scanned clipping capped at 16 s).
- Slow a shot to hold the clause's state rather than cut to the wrong picture.
- A short source forces reuse: spread the windows, play repeats as motion, make the last raw the longest.
- Never shave a shot or leave a 1-frame black gap; overlap instead.
- Pacing has a shape per section (open wide, tighten in the middle, open up for the payoff); held shots (2x median) are 57-72% of runtime.
- A repeated device in one case changes grammar the second time (plate, then card over footage), never the same shot twice in 20 s.
- A burned-in instrument readout (thermal, CCTV, bodycam stamp) is allowed when it is the clause's subject; the camera's own flaws stay as proof.
- Phone-vertical clips get a blurred fill behind; old 4:3 archival keeps clean black bars.
- Check each source for creator cards, captions, end cards, re-uploader overlays and watermarks before picking ranges; re-scan after any extension.
- A crop that leaves a fragment of creator text is worse than none; anchor it so none shows.
- After any hand edit by the owner, re-derive the clause map from real positions; the owner's own placements also get checked.
- Check every raw out-edge against the word it ends on so a cut never lands inside a word.
- The last line of a paragraph that teases the next beat gets one or two teaser shots of that moment.
- Never cut mid-speech in a raw; raw clips start and end on word edges (use word timings).
- Never cross the source creator's own edit, and leave no stray 1-10 frame fragments of another shot (including raw tails).
- Evidence beats: hold uncut, slow the replay, push in slowly; arrows or circles only when the target is certain (track it if it moves).
- Jump-cut dead air inside a raw clip; extend raws at word boundaries to hit the target runtime.
- Pack the case start: before the first raw, layer 5-8 real details (source page, date, channel, location, document or photo, teasers).
- Preview stills of every new device against the reference still before rendering; fix size, position and timing.
- When the user reports a problem at a timestamp, find the exact cause and fix it everywhere, not only there.
- Narration cut points keep at least 120 ms lead and about 400 ms tail before a raw.
- Never play a source range containing an internal cut; when the source runs out use another angle of the same scene.
- Every animation fully enters then holds readable: at least 1.5 s plus 0.3 s per word, total at least 3 s (pages 4-8 s, maps 3-5 s, name tag 2.1-2.9 s); entries 10+ frames.
- Device repetition limits: series devices repeat every case; page treatments 3-4 uses each; everything else at most about 5 per video and never in consecutive cases.
- When a repetitive device is removed, refill the spot with a new situation-fitting device if the narration explains, names, counts, dates, locates or compares something the footage does not show.
- A designed plate never opens empty or sits still: first element lands within about 8 frames of the cut, sparse graphics drift at a visible rate.
- Replays are real-time (no half-speed or frame doubling), with a crop or angle change, entered 0.2 s after the last word.
- Cut B-roll only at a sentence end or when the narration changes topic, on the pause midpoint or the word boundary, never by feel or on a round number.
- Change the picture on the spoken noun: each clause gets the literal picture of what it names, and the picture must not run a shot ahead of the voice.
- One continuous scene is one clip: do not chop it into short cuts, and fill a removed cut by extending the neighbouring clip.
- Pull the raw clip's head back so its picture runs ahead of its own audio when the narration is only describing what the raw clip is about to show.
- Do not fill narration gaps with frozen frames; replay the source as motion (a frozen talking face reads as a broadcast fault).
- In vlog footage the face dominates, so the non-face seconds are the fill budget; raw footage may run out and leave unavoidable black.
- Generic pacing: B-roll under narration changes every 2-4 s, nothing static past about 7 s without a reason, cut on motion, and about 90% of cuts are hard cuts.
- Hold a B-roll beat for the time needed to read the picture; a plate or highlight runs 3-4 s, max 5 s, and a longer beat is split into two clips at different camera angles.

## 9. Transitions

Most edits are straight cuts (31 of 34 in the 60 s sample); a straight cut is not a transition. Each transition has one job (rules 3 and 9): VHS for a chapter change, dip to black for a new date, place or time period, crossfade inside a montage, glitch when something breaks. VHS transition is one group of 15 variants, each with its built-in SFX. Crossfade and dip to black have no SFX.

- Cut straight unless one of the jobs below applies.
- Mark a chapter or case change with a dip to black into the title card. Use a VHS transition only rarely (an article or a page). *(set by you)* — see v03 · VHS tape start; v03 · VHS rewind to blue screen
- **VHS transition**: One group. When a rule says VHS, pick any one below (or the tape start / rewind from the references). Each plays its built-in SFX: keep it, change only the level. Never use Color Bars or Shaky Flashy (too loud).
  - Color Channel Offset: low hum that swells into a distorted warble, then fades (turn down 4 dB)
  - Static & Skew: steady crackling static with a buzz under it, flat level
  - Warp & Flicker: two soft ticks, then a low warble that builds
  - Flicker With Static: a steady buzz chopped on and off with the flicker
  - Warp Bars: bright hiss that swells at the end
  - Quick Flicker: short low thump (bass blip) (turn down 3 dB)
  - Quick Static: short static zap
  - Seeing Double: steady high tape whine (about 2 kHz)
  - Skipping Warp: a buzz that stutters 2-3 times as the frame skips
  - Warp Tracking: flat tracking hiss that jumps up at the end
  - Color Bleed: short bright white-noise hiss
  - Stretch Warp: hiss and whine that rise from quiet to loud (limit the click at the end)
  - Static Woosh: low rumbling woosh that builds (turn down 4 dB)
  - Wavy Burst 1: short buzzy burst (the same sound as Wavy Burst 2) (turn down 3 dB)
  - Wavy Burst 2: short buzzy burst (the same sound as Wavy Burst 1) (turn down 3 dB) *(set by you)* — examples: [Color Channel Offset.mp4](media/20f9d3f8d2af4ed2.mp4), [Static & Skew.mp4](media/d09b1d18c9524a34.mp4), [Warp & Flicker.mp4](media/2e15bf7cf73c44c3.mp4), [Flicker With Static.mp4](media/9ae5a5e5faec4ba3.mp4), [Warp Bars.mp4](media/b5a4be4a2284404b.mp4), [Quick Flicker.mp4](media/9dd8f075e60e4391.mp4), [Quick Static.mp4](media/33baf30dad564506.mp4), [Seeing Double.mp4](media/ed06195cd2ef440b.mp4), [Skipping Warp.mp4](media/0befd665d7a74648.mp4), [Warp Tracking.mp4](media/c5b3bf70401841a3.mp4), [Color Bleed.mp4](media/5546f4f5a7174108.mp4), [Stretch Warp.mp4](media/3606fa65970a4d51.mp4), [Static Woosh.mp4](media/1f9e92446da24e31.mp4), [Wavy Burst 1.mp4](media/720bf128f6714ef0.mp4), [Wavy Burst 2.mp4](media/a96f79483f09437a.mp4)
- Use a short glitch (1-4 s) when a broadcast cuts out or the story jumps. *(set by you)* — see v03 · Broadcast cuts out; v04 · Test card glitch; v01 · Dark blog posts, glitch transition
- Dip to black between sections: before a new date, place or time period. SFX: none. *(set by you)* — see v01 · Dip to black, gold date '2005/07/02'
- Crossfade between shots inside a montage; a light leak counts as a crossfade. SFX: none. *(set by you)* — see v01 · Light-leak transition, then blog card + gold 'Joe'; v01 · 'The Demons Have Taken Over' post + light leak
- Dip only at section handovers, about one per 50 s, not at every raw boundary.
- Dissolve the exits from evidence, hard-cut the entries into evidence so the riser lands; a clip under about 2.7 s takes one transition only.
- Dissolve and dip width is about 1.2 s (owner approved); never 2.0 s.
- A hard cut on the hook (cold open into first raw) is fine and needs no transition.
- Transitions never cross the creator's own cut; a plate needs material (handles) on both sides, about 0.6 s.
- Never judge a transition at its cut frame; sample inside it.
- Dissolve the exits out of raw evidence and hard-cut the entries into it, so the riser and impact land on the cut.
- The boundary between a B-roll montage and a raw clip is a dip to black of about 1-1.5 s, not a cross dissolve; dissolves stay inside the montage.
- Transition coverage percentage is an output of the policy, never a target to hit.
- Transition lengths that read right at 30 fps: whip 4-8 frames, dissolve 10-20, slow dissolve 30-45, fade to black 30-60; a transition that draws attention must be deliberate.
- **White flash**: A bright white flash that blooms into a reveal: an evidence page, a photo or a shock line. Full white for up to 10 frames, then it fades into the picture. Only into reveals, a few per video. SFX: a camera-flash pop or a low impact hit. *(set by you)*
- **Split-screen wipe**: A wipe that opens a side-by-side split of two clips. It may be used as any transition between shots. SFX: a short, low, soft whoosh. *(set by you)*

## 10. Typography

All added text is VCR OSD Mono (rule 2). The references use text sparingly: one-word chapter titles, years and dates, file-name labels and names, each centred and held for 2-4 s, plus on-screen typing into search boxes.

- Set every added title, date, label and caption in VCR OSD Mono (rule 2). *(set by you)* — see v04 · STATION922.MKV file label; v04 · 'БЕЗНОГNM' / 'LEGLESS' label
- Chapter titles are one or two words in capitals, centred over blurred, darkened footage. — see v03 · HOOLIGANISM title; v05 · Title 'ARAB GHOST HUNTING'; v03 · Red '1991' title
- Label names, years and titles in gold; file names and translations of foreign text in white. — see v01 · Mugshot footage + gold 'Joe' label; v05 · Third video page, title translated
- Show searches by typing them into the real search box, letter by letter. — see v01 · Typing 'google.com' in Wayback search; v01 · Typing 'fifthnail.blogspot.com' in Wayback
- Draw and look at the highlight rectangle on the source before rendering; quote the comment in full and let the highlight pick the claim.
- Highlight blend follows the page: screen on dark, multiply on light; red on dark, yellow on light.
- Spell proper nouns from the source's title or description, never from the transcript; list place names for caption casing.
- A title matches the shot under it and lands on the word that names the place.
- A title on a bright plate needs a scrim; move it off a chyron.
- Text safe area: 80 px from the sides, 100 px top/bottom at 1080p; headline at least 84 px, supporting at least 44 px.
- Titles and overlays fade in and out, never pop; raw subtitles and small notes cut hard on and off.
- Delete caption fragments and captions that overhang the raw ("And.", half sentences).
- Each case opens on the project's case title card (PROJECT/graphics/hyperframes/out/camping8/v3/card4-cN.mp4): the case's own footage, darkened with a vignette, a small gold VCR 'CASE N' over a big white condensed title, 4.5 s. Dip to black into it and out of it.
- Never show a creator's description when it holds personal or payment data.
- Captions are for creator speech only, never the narration; hand-fix every transcription error; bleep profanity with a dash in the caption.
- A label's form follows its meaning (place = map or HUD callout, date = data row, person = anchored tag, number = one still big number, never a counter); never the same lower-third twice in a row.
- Text is always native editor text; never a static title card, the title is a wall of tiles that flip to clips on the words.
- Speaker-anchored captions on raws; name tag shown the first time a key person speaks or is named.
- Put the place name on every wide or aerial establishing shot, large with the region small beneath, in VCR OSD Mono.
- Keep titles at least 80 px from the sides (title safe about 90%); one idea per card.
- **Caption box**: Captions are for raw clip speech only, never the narration. Each caption sits in a solid black box: no drop shadow, no outline. Make it with Premiere's Text tool, in VCR OSD Mono. *(set by you)*
- **Kinetic text**: Moving (kinetic) text is allowed in two places only: VVSentenceFrames for prison sentences or a person's fate, and PhraseSlam or ShoutLines once per video for the single most chilling line. All other quotes stay calm. Always VCR OSD Mono. *(set by you)*
- **Tracked text on pages**: Added text may be tracked (stuck) to a word on a captured page, e.g. 'Subscribed' on a channel page under the footage. The added text stays in VCR OSD Mono. *(set by you)*
- No channel credit ('YouTube: channel') on raw clips.

## 11. Music and sound

Narration leads. Loudness is measured in LUFS (the average loudness of the whole mix on a loudness meter): the references sit at -17.6 to -14.4 LUFS, 4 of the 5 near -17. The voice is calm, 155-195 words per minute, with 4-8 pauses of 0.6 s or more per minute (median 0.8 s). Music is a low bed (8.4 dB under the voice in the 60 s sample). Raw clips bring their own sound, faded by rule 8.

- Master to -17 LUFS integrated; keep the voice clear and steady.
- Keep music 8 dB under the narration on the loudness meter, as a dark ambient bed, not a melody.
- Let the raw footage's own sound play when it is the evidence, with the narration silent. — see v05 · Witch video ending, source audio; v05 · Abdullah footage: doors and noises
- Leave a pause of 0.8 s after a disturbing line before the next sentence.
- Fade raw clip audio by rule 8. *(set by you)*
- **VHS transition SFX**: Every VHS transition plays the SFX built into it (static, hiss, buzz, warble or whine; see Transitions). Keep that SFX; only change its level. Keep it short, under the narration, and near the set median of -23.6 dB RMS. No VHS SFX may stand out as loud noise. *(set by you)*
- No creator audio under narration: B-roll over voice-over is picture only.
- When the beat is the raw clip, pre-lap its picture; do not cut away to the same scene; gaps under about 5 s are a head extension.
- Two raws after one prose block: the second gets no pre-roll.
- Choose each raw on what is said in it: the soundbite that corroborates the paragraph; quoted dialogue beats a timestamp hint.
- A raw after every paragraph (minimum 8 s), and a video never ends on narration over black.
- Let narration breathe: cut where the waveform rests, keep narrator pauses (comma 0.2 s, sentence 0.35 s, paragraph 0.5 s); never tighten more than about 15%.
- Narration is only 56-72% of runtime; leave footage audio and silence, long speech gaps are the style, do not fill them.
- Verify every narration take by transcript against the script before building.
- A verdict, a prayer or a plea is never scored: pick the silent beat from the content.
- A source peaking at 0 dB cannot be brought up with gain; measure mean and peak and let the owner choose.
- A raw picture keeps running about 1.25 s under the next narration with its audio ducked to -24 dB, and the creator's voice is never audible under narration.
- Tighten AI narration gaps: sentence ends 0.25-0.35 s, commas 0.15-0.20 s.
- Remove the source creators' background music but keep ambience and scares.
- Voice-over and clip speech never overlap; the music bed ducks but is never dead (never below -50 dB for 1.2 s).
- Music bed about -31 LUFS, 3-7 cues per case crossfaded 6 s; a chapter card is never digital silence.
- Score the audio starts (the J-cut entry) precisely, never randomly: risers end on the evidence entry, impacts start on it.
- Never add music or SFX unless asked; when asked, build it fully with sane static levels and no ducking.
- Never put music over a silent "raw"; use 1-2 bed sections from different parts of a track and never the same (track, start) twice; adjacent cases never open on the same track.
- House SFX levels: impact -8, sub -5, riser -10, suck -14, vhs -18, texture -24 dB; hottest element about -8.5 dB peak.
- SFX are atmosphere, not punctuation: cluster them before a new section instead of punching every cut.
- Vary the scare: no two hand-offs get the same treatment; save the biggest hit for the act break and finale.
- Mark the exits too: the return from evidence to narration gets its own low air-suck sound.
- Layer sound: a sub only on the biggest beats, a seamless room tone, one register sound naming the medium (tape click, radio static).
- Never drop a diegetic sound effect blind; look at the frames first.
- No SFX file repeats inside a series; reviewers hear the reuse.
- A texture SFX is earned only when the narration names the sound.
- SFX stay restrained and tied to transitions (impacts on flashes, whooshes on slides, glitch hits).
- SFX sit 6-8 dB under the voice-over; never invent SFX; rotate variants; look-here marks are silent.
- Level SFX to the raw voice-over; an SFX set 15-20 dB too loud is a rejected mix.
- Clips placed over narration are picture only: strip their audio (ffmpeg -an or delete the clips); muting the track is not enough.
- Match the level so narration and raw audio sit at 0 to -6 dB on the meter; bake the gain into the file and do not use clip gain or faders.
- Put room tone under everything so silence never sounds like a dropout; digital-silent chapter cards were heard as an audio jump cut and now get a bed under each.
- Verify every narration take by transcribing the whole file and diffing it against the script; a wrong take can share its opening words.
- Narration is pre-stripped of silence by the owner; skip any automatic silence-cut phase.
- The voice is chosen per video; ask which voice, never assume the last one.
- Use one music track per video, extended to length by cross-fading the track into itself, never two stitched tracks.
- Keep music bass-heavy and dark: roughly 25 cues per video, centroid near 260 Hz, bed near -17.7 dBFS.
- Score the hand-off between a narration passage and an evidence block with a riser ending on the evidence entry and an impact starting on it; read the audio starts, not the video cuts.
- Place risers where the script says 'watch closely' or 'listen', not randomly.
- Vary the beats and escalate the impacts; a formulaic repeat was rejected, and the biggest impact goes on the act break and the final block.
- Leave one hand-off per case unscored, chosen from what the block says (a legal verdict, a prayer, a plea, a line where silence is the answer).
- Every SFX clip is a different file (127 unique), each baked to its own level.

## 12. Storytelling

An investigation told in order of discovery: a cold open on the most disturbing material, the narration posing the question over raw clips, then the evidence trail (searches, archived pages, comments, broadcasts) one step at a time, chapter titles at each turn, and a narrated sign-off with credits. No host on camera: the whole video is narration over raw clips.

- Open cold on the most disturbing footage, broken up with glitch tears, before any introduction; then let the narration pose the question over raw clips. — see v05 · Cold open: jinn footage, glitch tears; v03 · VHS tape start
- Follow the evidence in the order it was found: search, archived page, post, comment, footage. — see v01 · Typing 'fifthnail.blogspot.com' in Wayback; v01 · Wayback calendar for discord.com, push to 1996; v01 · r/scottandtomoko post with news link
- Name each chapter with a short title card. — see v03 · HOOLIGANISM title; v03 · Fight Back title
- Close the video on the thesis image, held as live footage not a freeze.
- End on the next case's picture when the narration turns to it (teaser).
- Verify the narration against footage before planning picture; search the case before illustrating it; use a different true document if the true one contradicts the beat.
- Open each case with a dense, layered opener; the intro is a teaser montage with every cut on a narration word.
- Send the first one or two cases for approval before doing the rest.
- Case title card: use the project's card design (card4-cN.mp4), case footage darkened under a small gold VCR 'CASE N' and a big white condensed title, 4.5 s, with a dip to black before and after it.
- Build the picture to the script: if narration names a place or document you cannot source, change the beat instead of showing a lookalike, since an uncaptioned stand-in still reads as the named thing.
- Cover the destination the narration names, never the walker, so the picture survives a re-record.
- Never fabricate a document about a real place or institution; say nothing on screen about a staged origin when the owner decides so.
- Run the reference analysis first and never edit from a text description of a reference.

## Motion graphics (which one, when)

Every built device shows a real artifact: a page, a date, a place, a URL, a comment. Devices enter on a hard cut (0 frames) and ride the shot's own slow linear push (WarpCard is the one exception: warp slide-in). Never: kinetic typography (except VVSentenceFrames for sentences or fate, and one PhraseSlam or ShoutLines per video), burned captions or word pops (except black-box captions on raw clip speech), particles, light leaks, charts or counters (one still big number is fine), tracked graphics (except added text tracked to a word on a captured page), 3D objects, invented infographics. To pick one: find what the narration is doing in the table below, then take the first graphic that fits. Skip "no" items; apply the change an "adapt" item names.
