Use it only if the video ends on credits. | Gives credit where it is due and closes the video with a calm, dark beat. | The video ends on the last narration line. Use Source label (g-376107b9) for single credits. | adapt: set names in VCR OSD Mono; no heart or icon art; slow scroll on black; credit real sources only. |
|  | NoticeCard | A notice inside the video: a content warning, a skip-time note, an 'epilogue' or a disclaimer. For frame 0 use Disclaimer card (g-3b4c99d9). | Tells the viewer what is cut or what is next, in plain text. | The text is already on screen. Do not repeat it. | adapt: set the text in VCR OSD Mono; red for the key word only; put it over a dark textured plate. |
| Hide or censor something | Redaction reveal | A document or message where the narration reveals what was hidden. | Approved by the owner in the Motion Lab on 2026-11-10. | Use the bars only on text that the narration reads. | yes |
|  | EyeBar | A victim or a minor is introduced by name and you have a face photo. Put the bar over the eyes while the narration says the name. | Protects the person, and it still shows that this is a real human. The viewer links the name to the face. | Do not use it on an adult suspect or a public figure. Use MaskFill when you have no photo. | yes |
|  | Blur patch (noc04_blur_patch) | The narration refers to a face, a name or text that you must hide. Use it on raw footage or a page. For gore or a full clip, use the 404 censor family (g-9312d3b1). | Hides private or graphic detail and stays plain, so it does not break the mood. | Do not use it where black-box captions on raw speech are the style. Do not blur a detail the story needs. | yes |
|  | MaskFill | The narration speaks of an unnamed person, victim or suspect and you must not show the face. Use it instead of a blur when you want a calm, flat shape. | Hides the identity but keeps the sense of a person. The viewer feels the gap. | The person is already named and shown in a source. Use Photo push; for a face in raw video use Blur patch (g-8718a98d). | adapt: keep the white or red fill; use only gold and red accents (drop the two-tone look); the mask must be drawn by hand for each shot. |
|  | CensorSound | A sound is too violent to play or show, such as gunshots or screams. Put the censored word over a heavily blurred clip. | The viewer knows what the sound was without hearing the worst of it. The asterisks make the censoring part of the look. | Do not use it for a sound the viewer needs to hear (use SoundLabel). Do not use it to hide a picture (use EyeBar or the 404 censor family). | adapt: set the word in VCR OSD Mono, red on the black chip, not Times italic |
|  | 404 library: censor family (5) | The clip or photo shows gore or a face that must not be shown. Use Mosaic or blur for a part of the frame. Use CutAway or CensorCard when the whole shot is unshowable. | Protects the viewer and the person, and the cut tells the viewer something was hidden. | Do not blur what the narration needs to show. For a face in a photo use EyeBar; for a sound use CensorSound. | adapt: use a fixed or keyframed region for the blur or mosaic (no tracked graphic); set CensorCard and PosterCard text in VCR OSD Mono |
| Move between shots | FlashBloom | Cut into a reveal: an evidence page, a photo or a shock line. Use it only a few times per video. | A burst of white makes the reveal hit. | Do not use it between ordinary shots. Use a crossfade or a hard cut there. | yes |
|  | Old TV switch-off | Move between shots. | Approved by the owner in the Motion Lab (round 2) on 2026-11-10. | Use real footage stills, screenshots and documents. No film texture on the graphic itself. | yes |
|  | ScreenZoom | "...and on that screen": the shot pushes into a screen in the scene and cuts to the page or clip it shows. | Links the room to the screen, so the viewer follows from the scene to the evidence. | Do not use it when the scene does not show a screen. Do not use a smooth dissolve-zoom. | adapt: a slow linear push into the screen, then a hard cut or a white flash to the capture; no smooth zoom-through |
| Other | Replay pair: normal pass + slow crop | The key moment of a raw is fast, dark or small and the VO goes back to it. | Built and QC-passed in van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11; for future videos. | A tag that is not true (no BRIGHTENED on an unbrightened pass). | - |
|  | Chained map pins | The VO moves between two named places, or names a place then a nearby site. | Built and QC-passed in van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11; for future videos. | No place named (then rule 39 arrival clip). | - |
|  | Black hold (freeze gain 0) | The VO describes something unseen, the dark, or a pause before the reveal. | Built and QC-passed in van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11; for future videos. | Over 7 s; as filler when footage exists. | - |
|  | AUDIO ENHANCED label | A dark or quiet recording whose audio is the evidence. | Built and QC-passed in van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11; for future videos. | When the audio was not processed. | - |
|  | Red highlight box on object | The viewer must find a small detail: a figure, light, mark or object the VO names. | Built and QC-passed in van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11; for future videos. | Moving/zooming source without a freeze; on a bang or event with nothing to point at. | - |
|  | End fade to black + 3 s black | The video's last section ends with no next-case teaser. | Built and QC-passed in van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11; for future videos. | A section that ends on a teaser (use the teaser hard cut). | - |
|  | Teaser hard cut end | The VO bridge turns to the next case. | Built and QC-passed in van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11; for future videos. | The last section of the video. | - |
|  | Channel page with name box | Every case, when the VO names the creator or channel (rule 33). | Built and QC-passed in van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11; for future videos. | Before the channel is named; drifting off centre. | - |
|  | YT-dark thread panel | A real comment or creator reply that adds a fact the footage cannot show. | Built and QC-passed in van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11; for future videos. | Invented handles; non-Latin text in a font without those glyphs. | - |
|  | PIP opening + VHS search | The VO refers to how the video starts, then jumps to a later moment. | Built and QC-passed in van-camping-encounters 2026-11-11; for future videos. | When the moment is already on screen. | - |

### What each graphic looks like

- **Page scroll highlight** (page-3d): The web page fills the whole screen, seen through a fixed, very light lens: a slight bulge in the middle, faint colour fringes at the sides. The lens does not change. The page scrolls in one smooth move to the key line, which gets a highlight. power2.inOut, 3.4 s. *(set by you)*
- **Page stack dolly** (page-3d): Camera glides through three real pages hanging in dark space (news story, forum post, archived site, each with its own header bar). Slow camera drift; far pages soft and darker (depth blur); near pages blur and slide out past the frame edges. Ends on the third page sharp and centred, then a gold marker highlights its key line. power2.inOut, 5 s move. *(set by you)*
- **CRT monitor push** (page-3d): Page sits on an old CRT monitor; the camera pushes from 62 % to 170 % into the screen. No end transition: it holds on the full screen with no fade and no dip to black. power2.inOut, 4 s. *(set by you)*
- **Archive date scrub** (ui-typing): An old web page in an archive viewer. A gold box steps along the years, and the page changes with each year until it is gone. power2.inOut, .6 s. *(set by you)*
- **Redirect chain** (ui-typing): Where a link really goes. Each jump lands whole, one under the other, and the last one fails in red. power2.out, .4 s. *(set by you)*
- **Upload facts under the player** (ui-typing): The video sits small. Its upload date, views and channel status land under it as a data row. power3.out, .8 s. *(set by you)*
- **Open folder list** (ui-typing): A raw server folder list. The rows land one by one. The odd file gets a gold bar, and its size of 0 turns red. power2.inOut, .8 s. *(set by you)*
- **File info window** (page-3d): An old-computer file info window opens. Size, camera and date land. The impossible date gets a red underline. power3.out, .9 s. *(set by you)*
- **Contact sheet** (page-3d): Twelve frames from the tape in a grid. All but one go dim, then the camera moves in on the one frame with the figure. power2.inOut, 1.2 s. *(set by you)*
- **Photo comes out of the noise** (page-3d): A found photo starts washed out, blurry and grainy. It slowly clears, like it is being recovered. sine.inOut, 2.4 s. *(set by you)*
- **Microfiche reader** (page-3d): Old newspaper pages fill the whole screen and slide past fast, then stop on the one story. The camera zooms in on the key line. Everything else blurs and goes dark. Then the line gets a gold bar. expo.out, 2.6 s. *(set by you)*
- **Statement print-out** (page-3d): A witness statement feeds slowly out of a printer slot. The line that matters gets a red underline. sine.inOut, 2.4 s. *(set by you)*
- **Page plane** (page-3d): Screenshot of the real page on a 3D-angled plane. Edge depth-of-field blur and a vignette. Linear push-in +2.3..+7.3 %/s (typical +5), or tilt down -10..-17 %H/s to read a long page. Wide first, then a macro on the line that matters. Median 8.4 s (2.3-36.7 s). — see v01 · Airport website, tilt and scroll down; v02 · Early YouTube homepage; v04 · Russian wiki entry, scroll; v03 · Manifesto text tilt
- **UI recreation / typing** (ui-typing): A recreated search bar or page (Wayback, YouTube, Google, Translate). Text types letter by letter; a cursor clicks. Dry keyboard or click foley only when the picture shows the action. Median 8.3 s. — see v01 · Typing 'google.com' in Wayback search; v02 · Dating site dropdowns; v04 · Translating the sign
- **G9 Source end card pushed in** (text-card): Hoaxer's end card pushed in with vignette — examples: [MB-86 preview](media/0dd83a414f234158.jpg)
- **G21 Card over its own blur** (text-card): Blog post or cover centred on a blurred copy of itself — examples: [MB-95 preview](media/984393aa4dc94662.jpg)
- **MaskTitle** (title-card): The platform name as a title, with a drawn mask icon replacing one letter. It pushes in fast at about 3.5 %/s and then cuts. — examples: [MA-48 preview](media/1926f7f6040c4ed7.jpg)
- **RansomWindow** (ui-typing): A recreated lock dialog over an infected desktop, with a headline, paragraphs, payment line and live countdown timers. Screen flicker is optional. — examples: [MA-79 preview](media/90f4c61554af4b2a.jpg)
- **SlideDeck** (page-3d): A briefing slide on a dark ground with a classified banner at top and bottom, a logo row, a seal and title, and a flow of labelled boxes and clouds joined by arrows. It rolls slowly. — examples: [MA-80 preview](media/9b7bbda0f14d4506.jpg)
- **TerminalLog** (ui-typing): A console window (Kali style) over a desktop, or full frame. Output arrives in bursts and scrolls. A red margin note labels the step and a red hand-drawn ellipse rings the key line. — examples: [MA-82 preview](media/44c0bc030d6c4b42.jpg)
- **PhraseSlam / ShoutLines (kinetic quote)** (text-card): From the 404 quote family: the words of one line slam or shake onto the screen. VCR OSD Mono. *(set by you)* — examples: [MA-250 preview](media/6fd9a51d7b1e4d1a.jpg)
- **Comment focus pull** (comments): Comment card slides up while it goes from a 6 px blur to sharp and from 104 % to 100 % scale; footage behind dims to 42 %. power3.out, 1.3 s. *(set by you)*
- **Comment from depth** (comments): Comment card flies forward from deep in the frame (z -450 to 0, tilt 30 to 12 deg), 1.7 s cubic; the whole card then drifts in Y rotation -14 to 5 deg over 5 s, linear. *(set by you)*
- **Comment key-line sweep** (comments): After the card lands, a soft gold band (rgba 201,165,74 at .34) sweeps across the key line once, 1.0 s. *(set by you)*
- **Comment recede** (comments): When the next comment comes, the old card goes back (scale .86, blur 4 px) and fades while the new one slides up, 1.1 s. The blur behind stays on. *(set by you)*
- **Quote key-word light-up** (text-card): Quote is on screen in grey; key words turn warm white one by one (stagger .4 s). *(set by you)*
- **Quote red underline** (text-card): Red underlines draw under the key words, .6 s each, stagger .45 s. *(set by you)*
- **Translate in place** (comments): A Russian comment. A thin line passes down it and swaps the words to English as it goes. For the Russian and Arabic videos. power2.inOut, 1.2 s. *(set by you)*
- **Comment card** (comments): One comment per shot, over real footage from the case or on the real page it came from (prefer a capture that scrolls to the comment). Parent then reply: the card grows to fit (shape morph) with easing and the reply crossfades in. Eased fade and scale in and out; never pops off. Centred, fully on screen. Median 8.4 s. — see v03 · Reddit comment on the shot; v02 · Rap battle comments; v04 · Image board thread; v01 · G7 One blog comment isolated: first as a white comment
- **Quote card / read-out** (text-card): The quoted text full screen in white serif over a dark blurred photo, or the post itself tilted. The VO reads it with a filtered voice and the music bed drops out. — see v03 · Quote card: 'terribly depressed'; v01 · Blog post read-out 'Chicken Pot Pie', tilt; v01 · G25 Read-out: quoted text + filtered voice, bed out
- **FringeLines** (text-card): Lines of article text in an RGB-split sans or a ghost serif, drifting slowly over a plate or over the sea. — examples: [MA-67 preview](media/3e4a7cc6e93f4230.jpg)
- **ChatBubbles** (comments): A chat thread with message bubbles, tilted in 3D or flat. Messages show one after the other with times, on a slow push. — examples: [MA-85 preview](media/a67e530d5ed5410e.jpg)
- **IMessage** (comments): One text message in a bubble, on a card or inside a phone with contact name and time. It rides a slow tilt and push. — examples: [MA-89 preview](media/084b3b012b084f79.jpg)
- **TerminalPanel** (ui-typing): A terminal panel with speaker and message lines typed in. A second mode shows a row of numbered badges, one lit at a time. — examples: [MA-112 preview](media/a750e331872a432a.jpg)
- **LEMMiNO Kryptos SectionWall + PhraseLift** (text-card): Long transcript split into parts; chilling line rises out of the transcript with green glow
- **Typed quote (noc08_typed_quote_v2, noc08_typed_quote2)** (text-card): Pixel-font line typed letter by letter Variants: G20 Retro terminal text: White monospace text on black ('THE TIME IS UP'). — examples: [MB-31 preview](media/24b86c24b2aa4052.jpg), [MB-94 preview](media/665e863ffa0b43cd.jpg)
- **WarpCard** (map): A red #CF0609 card with a 12 px bent (pincushion) edge and glow, a two-tone place name, a slow -1.8 %/s linear pull-out. It enters on its own warp slide-in (GlitchStreak) and leaves on a white flash. *(set by you)* — examples: [MA-16 preview](media/909bb0b8bf7946d5.jpg)
- **Route between two places** (map): A gold line draws from one town to the other like a trim path, with a glowing tip. It starts slow, speeds up, and settles in. The second pin pops as the tip arrives, then the distance. power3.inOut, 2.2 s. *(set by you)*
- **Signal trace** (map): Thin white lines draw from server to server like a trim path, each with a glowing tip. Each line starts slow, speeds up, and settles in. Each point pops the moment the tip lands. The red ring pops only after the last line has fully reached its end. The last point is a red ring with "APPROX. LOCATION". Only use it if a source shows the path. power3.inOut, .9 s. *(set by you)*
- **Map / place card** (map): Real Google Maps place card, coordinates panel, satellite or Street View, on a dark background or full frame. Slow push or slide. Median 8.2 s. — see v01 · Google Maps place card + Street View; v04 · Coordinates on Google Maps; v03 · Sinclair stations map
- **PixelLetters** (map): Large letters made of glowing LED pixels sit in the scene. The shot then changes to a sepia satellite view of the place. — examples: [MA-94 preview](media/c2b74ea012984aee.jpg)
- **LocationStamp (overlay)** (text-card): A place name stamp over footage. The place is large, in capital letters. A smaller mono line sits under it (for example the date or coordinates). Variants: LocationStamp: Top-left stamp: place, date, detail. VCR location title: Centred near bottom: place big, sub-line small. — examples: [MA-216 preview](media/fe676cb5ad2c4106.jpg)
- **Year rise** (title-card): A gold line draws, then the year rises up out of a mask on the line. power3.out, 1.1 s. *(set by you)*
- **Date row** (text-card): DATE / PLACE / TIME cells come in one after another (stagger .16 s), each power3.out .8 s. *(set by you)*
- **Camcorder OSD date** (layout): Camcorder on-screen display in the corners: REC dot, date and a clock whose seconds tick. *(set by you)*
- **Timeline strip** (text-card): Four real pieces of proof stand in a row, each with its date above. The cards rise in one after another. The camera glides from one to the next in one smooth curve and never fully stops. Focus, size and turn change smoothly with distance: the card in focus is sharp and faces you, the others are soft, dark and turned in. The last date is red. power3.inOut, 1.2 s. *(set by you)*
- **Time jump card** (text-card): A short card for a jump in time: the new date, then "3 DAYS LATER" in gold, then a gold line. power2.out, .9 s. *(set by you)*
- **Rewind to an earlier day** (text-card): The real footage plays. Then REWIND: the same footage runs backwards fast, with tracking lines and a shaky picture. Then PLAY, the older date, and the earlier part of the tape plays. power1.inOut, 1.5 s. *(set by you)*
- **Year / chapter title** (title-card): Big gold or red serif word or year over a blurred freeze of the previous shot, or white monospace on a black bar. Fades or rises in, then rides the push. Median 2.7 s (1.6-8.4 s). — see v01 · Gold year title '1996' over blur; v03 · Fight Back title; v05 · Title 'ARAB GHOST HUNTING'
- **StockClause** (other): Black-and-white 4:3 stock shots, one per clause. A stamp lands on a shot: a year, a figure (for example $400.000) or red coordinates. The stamp blinks briefly. — examples: [MA-25 preview](media/3b99dd6fa3664768.jpg)
- **Glitch number (Glitch2025)** (glitch): RGB-split glitch where the last digit flips from one value to the next — examples: [MA-217 preview](media/70d357430ef94e40.jpg)
- **Date label, lower-left (noc02_date_label_v2)** (text-card): Serif date and time ('April 30th, 8:50 PM') at lower left Variants: DateLabel (c02_date): 'JUNE 2022' on a black plate, lower-left, slides in. VCR year stamp: Bottom-left year with small rider line. — examples: [MB-12 preview](media/e5f83f6541824dfc.jpg)
- **Corner brackets label** (text-card): Four corner brackets close in on the subject (scale 1.6 to 1, power3.out 1.0 s), then the name tag appears. *(set by you)*
- **Leader line label** (text-card): A thin leader line draws from the subject (.9 s), then a gold name and a white sub line come in. *(set by you)*
- **File window label** (layout): A file or record window opens from its centre line with a clip mask, power3.out 1.1 s, and shows the name or ID. *(set by you)*
- **Case dossier** (layout): Case-file folder: photo with a paper clip, a label strip, and a red UNVERIFIED stamp that lands with no bounce. *(set by you)*
- **Last seen card** (text-card): A photo print on the left. On the right: LAST SEEN in gold, then the date, the place and what they wore, one line at a time. power3.out, .9 s. *(set by you)*
- **Photo push** (other): Full-frame photo with a vignette and a slow linear push-in (+2.3..+7.3 %/s). Optional: push in to one face while the others darken and blur. Old photos stay black and white. — see v01 · Photo of Brewster at servers, push; v02 · Founders photo push; v04 · Hockey handshake photo
- **UiCardLift** (text-card): A user card cut from a captured page, lifted and shown large over a blurred and dimmed copy of the page. — examples: [MA-101 preview](media/d867cd712ccc4e70.jpg)
- **MonoEcho** (other): A dip to black (about 0.5 s out and 0.5 s up). The subject's shot comes up in mono and slowed, with 2 faint trailing ghost copies. A VCR OSD Mono name chip (white on black) sits beside the face. A list form stacks 2-4 chips. — examples: [MA-161 preview](media/4177a5a60a7a4fae.jpg)
- **PhotoNameBar** (other): A portrait with a slow push. A dark red bar sits low with the name in wide-spaced light type and a small corner tick. Two names can show on two boxes. — examples: [MA-6 preview](media/17eb0718e35c4f92.jpg)
- **AliasTile** (other): A small avatar tile, or a "?" tile for an unknown user, with the alias set beside it. The tile flashes for one frame as it cuts in. — examples: [MA-17 preview](media/06f9b936d3c44b9c.jpg)
- **NicknameRed** (other): The nickname in big red monospace type, centred over the person's face. The picture is blurred at the edges and sharp in the centre, with a slow push. — examples: [MA-57 preview](media/549c07a413c94956.jpg)
- **EmblemWord** (title-card): The name as a big word with its emblem: a laurel, a flag fill, a neon plate, or placed behind the subject. — examples: [MA-66 preview](media/98498240dc0e4657.jpg)
- **SilhouetteGroup** (other): Dark silhouette figures stand in a group on a dim ground. One figure is lit (red in the solo variant) and the others dim. — examples: [MA-72 preview](media/10b6ff0336fd4e7b.jpg)
- **AccountLadder** (other): A captured account page with a focus box on the profile. It steps to the profile photo, then to the person's name. The locked or tilted page rides a slow push. — examples: [MA-84 preview](media/3694afe7a94b408d.jpg)
- **FaceIdProfile** (other): A portrait with rows of pixel-font labels on the left and a red decision box on the right. The chosen face glows and the rest fade. The shot is defocused with RGB noise. — examples: [MA-88 preview](media/9735e50009a842f4.jpg)
- **NamesOnPhoto** (other): A real photo with a name beside each person. The edge is blurred and the photo has a vignette and slow push. — examples: [MA-93 preview](media/e814bc1ceac147df.jpg)
- **PhotoNames** (other): One, two or three photos side by side with a name under each, on a dark plate. Variants: Case cards: NocturnCouple + HCE-Couple: Two-person intro plate (couple/pair). — examples: [MA-148 preview](media/2a7ac5b59e3246d2.jpg), [MA-225 preview](media/2e94c65c915249c6.jpg)
- **VVRetroWindow** (other): A retro desktop window springs open on black, titled "visual venture". The portrait grows inside it. The person's name types on in a mono face with a blinking caret and a faint colour fringe. 3-4 s. Variants: VVRetroWindowGX: The upgrade of VVRetroWindow. It has a glossy bevel, a red and cyan colour edge on the left, top and bottom edges bowed like a CRT, and a horizontal glitch streak that flashes across the frame while the window opens. — examples: [MA-200 preview](media/34111800da54404e.jpg), [MA-207 preview](media/939f19132e504749.jpg)
- **Case cards: NocturnChannelPlate + HCE-ChannelPlate** (text-card): Channel/uploader plate with avatar and name — examples: [MA-224 preview](media/2b1bbe9020e64a94.jpg)
- **CCTV HUD** (layout): CCTV frame: CAM number, REC and date in the corners, plus a tracking box that follows the walking figure. *(set by you)*
- **Video in its page** (page-3d): The watch page on an angled plane with the video playing in its player. Linear push about +5.5 %/s toward the player or the view count. Vignette, soft edges. Variants: ChannelPage (c02_page): Dark channel page, pan to a tile, red box, zoom in, footage plays. — see v01 · Tilted YouTube page, view count; v05 · 'Ghost Car' YouTube page; v02 · Dog video watch page — examples: [MB-51 preview](media/abc18ac5679f4a3e.jpg)
- **PLAY OSD (noc08_play_osd_v2)** (other): VCR 'PLAY >' on-screen display, 0.33 s — examples: [MB-30 preview](media/d1bce9ea6ff34db9.jpg)
- **DeviceInsert** (layout): A phone frame sits in the centre third of the frame on a grey radial ground. App captures hold for 12 to 16 s and dissolve in 0.9 to 1.4 s. A rescreen variant shows the screen with sub-pixels. — examples: [MA-27 preview](media/7449b9a131804f36.jpg)
- **WindowFrame** (layout): The clip sits in a smaller window on near-black instead of filling 16:9. A phone variant shows a 9:16 window on dark grey-green. An optional teal black-and-white grade can be added. — examples: [MA-32 preview](media/b36da4ebd627461a.jpg)
- **RecOverlay** (other): A light-streak whip, then a huge REC with a blinking red dot on the footage. It can also sit in a corner or as red text. — examples: [MA-44 preview](media/d9179f1317c14f20.jpg)
- **ArchiveTreatment** (other): A photo or clip with a black-and-white, news or film grade, grain and slight blur. A place and date line sits below, with a source credit.
- **CallWave** (other): A line or bar wave of the audio runs across the frame, with a caption below. Speakers can have colour cues. — examples: [MA-143 preview](media/e63c04a4d51144ea.jpg)
- **VVBlurFill** (other): The vertical clip plays full height in the middle. The same clip, enlarged, blurred and scan-lined, fills the sides, with a dark falloff at the clip edges. A credit tag such as YT: NAME and a small caption sit on top. A print mode shows a landscape photo as a white-bordered print over its blur. — examples: [MA-198 preview](media/962ff93e6c544e2d.jpg)
- **404 library: footage family (10)** (layout): Ten templates in the 404 library: DashHold, CrtTv, PhonePanel, Replay, PipCam, Letterbox, AngleSync, RadioWave, FloatingClipCard. Each frames a clip in a TV, a phone, a small window or a replay. Variants: CrtBox: The clip plays inside a rounded CRT screen with barrel bend, grille lines, RGB split and vignette. It can be full size or an inset, and it has a slow push. — examples: [MA-238 preview](media/ac941914cc384023.jpg), [MA-62 preview](media/23964bcfe4c14a86.jpg)
- **Tracked word on a page ('Subscribed')** (page-3d): A captured page sits under the footage; one added word ('Subscribed') is tracked to its spot on the page. VCR OSD Mono. *(set by you)*
- **Red ring draw-on** (other): A red ring draws around the detail, .8 s. *(set by you)*
- **Iris spotlight** (other): Everything around the subject darkens to a soft spotlight. sine.inOut, 1.2 s. *(set by you)*
- **Punch-in with ring** (other): Slow push from 100 % to 128 % (power2.inOut 1.6 s), then a red ring draws on the detail. *(set by you)*
- **Red block arrow** (other): A red block arrow slides in and stops just short of the target. power3.out, .9 s. *(set by you)*
- **Line highlight** (page-3d): Pale yellow box (#DCD896, multiply blend) over the read line. It grows from the line centre outward over 14 frames (power1.inOut), starting 0.25 s before the quoted words. Rides the page plane's push. Variants: G24 Calendar year square: A coloured square sits on one day of a real Wayback calendar page. The page pushes in slowly. The source marks this as low confidence. — see v01 · Its a 3d pan zoom with a highlighting effect; v04 · View count highlight; v05 · HuffPost article, Lancashire highlight; v03 · Article: hostage negotiators — examples: [MB-98 preview](media/fd5961a82bb04e1c.jpg)
- **Mono label over blur** (title-card): White monospace type on a black box rises in over a blurred copy of the page or thread. Can swap to the English translation in place. — see v04 · STATION922.MKV file label; v04 · 'БЕЗНОГNM' / 'LEGLESS' label; v02 · Video in question blocked
- **SoundLabel** (text-card): A sound cue in VCR OSD Mono on a tight black box at bottom centre, for example *Josh hears footsteps*. It holds about 4.5 s and cuts in and out with the shot. — examples: [MA-197 preview](media/6d118a8d0c8f45ea.jpg)
- **Freeze-push with red circle** (other): Last frame frozen, red circle on subject, slow push, then un-freezes Variants: AnalysisFreeze: The clip freezes or slows in mono. A red ring or white box marks the detail, with a VCR label. The picture then cuts to colour 0.4 to 0.56 s after the last word. — examples: [MA-152 preview](media/1b3a34c7d4724e90.jpg)
- **CurvedArrow** (page-3d): A hand-drawn curved arrow (red, or white on dark footage) draws itself in over a few frames and ends with a head on the named item. It drifts slightly with the shot. — examples: [MA-4 preview](media/8f5924d8d67841cc.jpg)
- **CctvReframe** (other): The CCTV clip is re-framed in steps: punch-ins to a crop, short tints, and in one case a double exposure of a second image over the clip. — examples: [MA-34 preview](media/c94a45f149f447a3.jpg)
- **CircleCallout** (other): A hand-drawn ring that draws on over a figure in leaked CCTV. A second variant is a black bar over the eyes. — examples: [MA-61 preview](media/96e9cf723acd40bf.jpg)
- **HudTag** (other): A small bracket label with the name of the object, placed on the shot. It types in and the brackets close around it.
- **Replay variants (4: SlowReplay, FrameStep, VcrReplay, AdjustedReplay)** (other): Same clip replayed slower, frame by frame, on VCR noise, or colour-adjusted — examples: [MA-135 preview](media/cd5579c77c0441df.jpg)
- **Loupe** (other): A red ring marks an area of the playing clip. A zoomed inset of that area shows beside it, and the rest of the frame dims. — examples: [MA-138 preview](media/0ae04b7d4f1c40cf.jpg)
- **SpotGlow** (other): The frame turns to mono. The figure keeps its colour and gets a soft glow, held for about 10 s. — examples: [MA-140 preview](media/97d64cdf8b4b42d4.jpg)
- **PaperFrame** (layout): The playing shot shrinks inside a light paper border with a thin dark keyline. A handwritten conclusion writes on, either white inside the shot or dark ink on the paper below. The camera drifts slowly. The frame can grow back to full. — examples: [MA-162 preview](media/f8c3a187183a4b75.jpg)
- **ShotNote** (text-card): The shot goes mono, holds, then a white marker conclusion writes on in the lower left at a steep angle, in step with the spoken line. An arrow draws to the subject. A tilt version puts the frame on paper. — examples: [MA-165 preview](media/121ef0c2512445dc.jpg)
- **ArrowLabel** (text-card): A thick red arrow with a bold caps label (for example VICTIMS SLEEPING), or thin red leader lines with lower-case *asterisk* labels. Everything pops in on one frame and holds across cuts. Silent. Variants: EdgePointer: A solid red block arrow (about 300 px) points down-left at the subject. It pops in on one frame and can carry a short label. — examples: [MA-190 preview](media/e21569e75ac54487.jpg), [MA-136 preview](media/543a5fd7687f4f96.jpg)
- **KW frame-circle** (other): Still of a figure with an animated ring drawn round it Variants: LEMMiNO Kennedy PhotoMarkup + LineupStage: Pointers/boxes on an archival photo; silhouette police line-up. Radar rings (noc02_radar_rings): Red rings pulse out over a dark photo. — examples: [MA-221 preview](media/6002f55692744a97.jpg), [MA-127 preview](media/fef884dab1404b99.jpg), [MB-34 preview](media/be6200b3d530450a.jpg)
- **Excerpt heading (noc11_ex1_heading_v3)** (text-card): Big white/red words pulled from a page, rest faded — examples: [MB-4 preview](media/d5ca85e5a50c40d6.jpg)
- **Freeze label (noc07_freeze_label)** (text-card): A raw frame freezes. A thin white box draws round one spot and a short label names it in a pixel font. The label sits next to the box. — examples: [MB-28 preview](media/ba0987ce35d040ab.jpg)
- **VVSentenceFrames** (text-card): Big text frames, one per person, with a whip between them: '12 YEARS IN PRISON' -> whip -> '5 YEARS IN PRISON'. VCR OSD Mono. *(set by you)* — examples: [MA-201 preview](media/942b92fb1c9f415e.jpg)
- **FigureCard (one big number)** (text-card): One huge still number on a dark ground with a slow push. VCR OSD Mono. Variants: Case cards: NocturnStakes + HCE-Stakes: Plate listing what is at stake. *(set by you)* — examples: [MA-226 preview](media/db21d900b86c4b8a.jpg)
- **Number with line and unit** (text-card): Number lands whole (power2.out 1.0 s), a gold line draws under it, then the unit appears. *(set by you)*
- **Case status** (text-card): The case name, a gold line, then what is known, one row at a time. A red UNSOLVED stamp lands last. power3.out, .5 s. *(set by you)*
- **Case counter** (text-card): CASE 3 in gold over five small boxes. Done cases are filled, and box 3 fills gold now. Tells the viewer how far in they are. power2.inOut, .8 s. *(set by you)*
- **PunchCard** (text-card): One line of large text, centred on black or on a plate, with one word bold or red. It can build in italic words and dissolves into an image. — examples: [MA-51 preview](media/b7483b29582b45aa.jpg)
- **FootageNumber** (other): A thin number or short phrase (for example "20 meters deep") inside 4:3 CCTV. In the red variant a red "34" stands over a silhouette while the spot light drops to about 11 %. — examples: [MA-55 preview](media/706da80a2fce4132.jpg)
- **NumberToSource** (other): A giant number (for example "50") stands as a dark silhouette. It dissolves into the news page that gave the number. — examples: [MA-69 preview](media/4ba704bac9f645e9.jpg)
- **LogoMelt** (glitch): One logo melts and stutters into a second logo, with a short defocus. The picture then settles on the new logo. — examples: [MA-90 preview](media/6046864e44a94d91.jpg)
- **Upgrade targets, other (StepRamp, MeasureOnSat, MeasureOnPhoto, FloatingClipCard** (text-card): Four templates. StepRamp: a stepped freeze ramp (slow build-up, then 2-3 exact-frame holds). MeasureOnSat and MeasureOnPhoto: a dashed red bracket with a typed value on a satellite image or photo. FloatingClipCard: a small clip card floating over its own blur. — examples: [MA-256 preview](media/d702ebc984724b25.jpg)
- **Outcome chip / stack (noc08_outcome_chip, noc08_outcome_stack_v3)** (other): One or more dark chips hold lines of pixel text, for example 'Lifetime Ban On Possessing Firearms'. The stack version shows several lines together. — examples: [MB-29 preview](media/2cb3c0af7a76410d.jpg)
- **Split-screen wipe** (layout): A wipe that opens a side-by-side split of two clips. *(set by you)*
- **2.5D parallax collage** (layout): Photo and page cut-outs on layers at different depths drift past at different speeds. One sine.inOut ease, 5.5 s. *(set by you)*
- **Split screen / grid / card row** (layout): Two clips side by side, photos as vertical panels, or a row of thumbnails or cards. Blurred edges, vignette, slow pan or push. Median 13.2 s. — see v01 · Split screen: remote + hotel room; v04 · Split: video vs screenshots; v03 · Three acquitted faces; v02 · Elsagate thumbnail rows
- **StockMontage** (other): A run of stock shots, one per noun in a spoken list, each cut on the word time. The grade can switch from normal colour to crime B/W at a chosen shot. — examples: [MA-30 preview](media/8382fa3b317d4115.jpg)
- **PinBoard** (layout): Photos and papers pinned or taped on a board, joined by red string. A mugshot can pop on, and a postcard can carry a handwritten place. Grounds are cork, a green mat or a wall. Variants: Evidence board (noc01_evidence_board_v2; v1 nocturne_evidence_board): Photos pinned and joined by thin red lines, slow move. — examples: [MA-50 preview](media/6f2a54cd7dae40ca.jpg), [MB-13 preview](media/c2ecbc912ca44207.jpg)
- **DataList** (text-card): A heading and a column of data items on a dark ground, drifting slowly. Variants: blue breach, red alert and green terminal. — examples: [MA-63 preview](media/91cfabe489954b87.jpg)
- **CutoutPop** (layout): Cut-out pictures of items (a jacket, a shoe) appear one by one over a frosted map or scene background. — examples: [MA-87 preview](media/aa56b60485d249a0.jpg)
- **MethodCards** (text-card): Title cards for each item enter one after the other and stay on screen. The shots behind them change.
- **LinkMap** (map): A full-frame page capture gets a red frame and zooms out into the centre card of a node graph. Red lines run to other page cards that enter from outside the frame. Dark red vignette. It holds for about 3 s, then a hard cut. Variants: Link board (noc06_link_board_v3): Thick red rounded frame joining screenshot panels. — examples: [MA-159 preview](media/3f9740be67d642e7.jpg), [MB-16 preview](media/ef9a93989c6e414a.jpg)
- **ScrapBoard** (layout): Scrapbook board on grey paper, three layouts. Annotate: writing on the shot, then the camera pulls back and an arrow draws to a second still. Pair: two stills with a curved arrow and a line like "Same person?". Grid: a 2x2 grid of bordered stills with labels, then a fifth still. — examples: [MA-164 preview](media/ce0cc26739624f23.jpg)
- **camping8: channel-plate, channel-v3, dossier, theories, side-by-side, ir-replay** (other): Six hyperframes files: channel-plate, channel-v3, dossier (Courier and Geo text), theories (Bebas and VCR), side-by-side (two clips) and ir-replay (an infrared replay with a rewind mark). — examples: [MA-233 preview](media/11cf218cf4154038.jpg)
- **404 library: evidence family (11)** (layout): Eleven templates in the 404 library, including Corkboard, DeskSpread, StackFlyThrough, TiltedWall, SplitCompare, CitationSheet and CardWall. They show several documents or photos on a board, a desk, a wall or a stack. — examples: [MA-241 preview](media/5d8db55705bf4ce7.jpg)
- **Analysis board card + pan (noc01_board_card_v3, noc01_board_pan, nocturne_analys** (layout): A pale board sheet. Cards scale in one by one. The camera pans across the board. (Files: noc01_board_card_v3, noc01_board_pan, nocturne_analysis_board.) — examples: [MB-14 preview](media/eeeeb1d69a124e1f.jpg)
- **CCTV wall zoom (noc01_cctv_wall_zoom; v1 nocturne_cctv_wall_zoom)** (layout): Many camera feeds as a wall, zoom to one — examples: [MB-17 preview](media/d6b8dfca69e64151.jpg)
- **Inset clip (noc13_inset)** (other): Video inset with white frame border over footage — examples: [MB-22 preview](media/fbc23a13401f4801.jpg)
- **Title tracking settle** (title-card): Title letters start wide apart (letter-spacing .5em) and close to .12em. power3.out, 1.8 s. *(set by you)*
- **Title depth focus** (title-card): Title goes from a 10 px blur and 108 % scale to sharp and 100 %. power2.out, 1.4 s. *(set by you)*
- **Title glint** (title-card): One gold light glint sweeps across the title after it lands. sine.inOut, 1.6 s. *(set by you)*
- **VHS tape label** (title-card): A real-looking VHS tape (thick 3D shell, ribbed plastic, tape wound on the reels, a worn crooked label, a spine label) floats in from the dark and turns slowly while a soft light slides over it. For stories about a tape. It does not replace the case card. power2.inOut, 1.8 s. *(set by you)*
- **Please stand by card** (glitch): PLEASE STAND BY card settles in from a vertical roll, with one tracking line passing. *(set by you)*
- **Open questions** (text-card): STILL UNANSWERED, then one question at a time. Each older question goes grey when the next one lands. power2.out, .6 s. *(set by you)*
- **CASE N card** (text-card): The project's case title card (card4-cN.mp4): case footage darkened with a vignette, small gold VCR 'CASE N', big white condensed title, 4.5 s. Dip to black in and out. — examples: [MB-32 preview](media/3892c43cf6a246c1.jpg)
- **G1 Fade up from black** (transition): Whole-frame fade up over 48 f into the first page — examples: [MB-79 preview](media/f2de552090b64b72.jpg)
- **ChannelSting** (title-card): The channel name appears on a dark ground with a soft wipe, holds, and then drops away. Variants show 'presents', 'welcome back' or a typed wordmark. — examples: [MA-113 preview](media/64bcf2ae8b634ffd.jpg)
- **RedSun** (title-card): A red sun or moon rises above a dark horizon and shrinks, with a halo and a caption. In the outro it sits over the end credits. — examples: [MA-120 preview](media/fd4f44e95a10490a.jpg)
- **TitleChips** (title-card): Two-line title on chips over the playing wall of clips. Line 1 is light grey on a dark chip. Line 2 is red on a black chip. VCR OSD Mono caps. It enters with a 3-4 frame pixel drop-out, holds about 2 s, then cuts out. — examples: [MA-177 preview](media/c766f28a1e1c4fcb.jpg)
- **Numbered case grid (noc10_case_grid, noc10_case_grid2_v3)** (layout): Six panels with red numbers 1-6 — examples: [MB-20 preview](media/883485ae52d945e8.jpg)
- **Chapter card with kicker + rule** (text-card): Black, kicker, big number, thin white rule, fades
- **Colour-split title settle** (glitch): Title starts as a red and a blue copy offset to the sides; they slide together into one clean white title. power3.out, 1.3 s. *(set by you)*
- **Archive terminal** (ui-typing): Dark archive terminal. Each line lands whole; the last line is red (for example ARCHIVE CORRUPTED). The cursor does not blink. *(set by you)*
- **Video goes dead** (other): The video plays, then goes dark and soft, and the real "Video unavailable" screen fades up over it. sine.inOut, 1.0 s. *(set by you)*
- **Broken file bytes** (glitch): The raw bytes of the file land line by line. The empty, broken parts turn red. The last line says what is missing. sine.inOut, .6 s. *(set by you)*
- **Glitch / static** (glitch): Matrix rain, RGB tearing, VHS tracking static, test card or colour bars, as an overlay or a short burst. Median 3.8 s (0.8-7.7 s). — see v01 · Wayback home + green matrix overlay; v03 · VHS tape start; v04 · Test card glitch
- **G23 Red error banner** (other): Native 'This channel does not exist' banner — examples: [MB-97 preview](media/4091470b01aa4b76.jpg)
- **RedWashCut** (transition): A hard cut that floods the frame with red and a soft blur. The wash decays fast and the new shot sharpens. A white bloom variant exists. — examples: [MA-8 preview](media/6b27a5d9ea774461.jpg)
- **StatusGlyphs** (other): Phone status icons (signal, wifi, battery). One signal bar pings and then goes dark, or a call rings out and stops. — examples: [MA-52 preview](media/f3f44507f0244d37.jpg)
- **DeniedScreen** (ui-typing): A recreated system screen: a big [ACCESS DENIED], a red console, or an admin login panel. The camera is slightly out of focus at the edges. — examples: [MA-65 preview](media/825a91d082c44561.jpg)
- **ThresholdDuotone** (other): A photo turned into a two-colour print with hard contrast and film grain. The ink is red or white on black. — examples: [MA-99 preview](media/4f8d939d4d3e4806.jpg)
- **DreadWash** (glitch): A light page tints to saturated red over about 1 s (the detail stays). Thin scan-noise streaks run through it. It ends on a 3-6 frame TV-snow burst, then a hard cut or black. — examples: [MA-156 preview](media/778b9eacf6d8478d.jpg)
- **Source label / editor note** (other): Gold #cda75c lowercase humanist sans, bottom-left (left 1.2 %W, bottom 2.1 %H), 3.4 %H tall; editor note fades in 1.2 s ease-out. Source label #d09f61 at 75 % opacity, cuts in at 0 frames. — see v01 · Mugshot footage + gold 'Joe' label
- **WarningSlate** (other): A dark slate with a small warning triangle, or a red warning sign over blurred black-and-white footage. A date can sit on the same slate. — examples: [MA-59 preview](media/3033534f511c4137.jpg)
- **DisclaimerCard** (text-card): White text lines on black with a little flicker and bloom. Key phrases show in colour. It holds, then cuts to black. — examples: [MA-114 preview](media/834c7bf4d5e34f15.jpg)
- **NoticeList** (text-card): A heading and a short list of notices in monospace type, with smeared edges and dropouts, in the cold open. — examples: [MA-117 preview](media/f969278a45754638.jpg)
- **RatingSlate** (text-card): A rating box (TV, MA) with a header, a footer and a list of descriptors, on a plate with a slow push. — examples: [MA-119 preview](media/57800cb58f82456e.jpg)
- **EndCredits** (title-card): Names and short cards scroll up the frame at a steady speed, with small insets beside them. — examples: [MA-145 preview](media/e9a94d4443764cb8.jpg)
- **NoticeCard** (text-card): One or more lines of text in the middle of the frame, with one accented word. Several pages can follow each other. Variants: Red warning card: Black, red box: 'WARNING / VIEWER DISCRETION IS ADVISED'. — examples: [MA-146 preview](media/23a263148d974e10.jpg)
- **Redaction reveal** (censor): Black redaction bars slide away one at a time (.8 s each, stagger .6 s) to show the hidden words. *(set by you)*
- **EyeBar** (censor): A solid black bar over the eyes on a full-frame face photo. The bar belongs to the photo and moves with it during a slow push. It is in from frame 0. A black-and-white threshold print version exists. — examples: [MA-157 preview](media/5b92da0c69a84bc5.jpg)
- **Blur patch (noc04_blur_patch)** (censor): Blurred patch over part of the frame — examples: [MB-33 preview](media/c21a560fabc145f5.jpg)
- **MaskFill** (censor): A person in the shot is filled with a flat white or red shape. The edge is soft and can glow. The shape can dissolve back to the photo. — examples: [MA-91 preview](media/860286d8328048df.jpg)
- **CensorSound** (censor): The clip is blurred (sigma about 40 px) with a dark vignette. A black chip sits at the centre with a red censored word such as (g*ns**ts). A second form shows the clip in a 4:3 inset window on near-black. Hard cut in and out. — examples: [MA-191 preview](media/206a501ab1dd4ff5.jpg)
- **404 library: censor family (5)** (censor): Five templates in the 404 library: TrackedBlur, Mosaic, CutAway, CensorCard and PosterCard. They hide gore or a face. Variants: CensorMarks: Two forms. TrackedMosaic: hard-edged mosaic blocks (about 65 px) over a region of the footage. RedactedDoc: a light article page under a dark vignette with a slow push, solid black bars over names, and a red marker bar that wipes behind the key phrase. — examples: [MA-251 preview](media/1d12734df0364adf.jpg)
- **FlashBloom** (transition): A white camera-flash exposure that blooms over the frame (full white up to 10 frames) and settles on an evidence page or photo. *(set by you)* — examples: [MA-173 preview](media/df271fbd71174d87.jpg)
- **Old TV switch-off** (transition): First the tape breaks up: torn lines slide sideways, the picture jumps, static and a rolling noise bar come in. Then it switches off like a real old TV: still shaking, the picture flares white and snaps into one bright line, the line pulls in to a glowing dot, and the dot slowly fades (afterglow). NO SIGNAL fades up. For a case that ends cold. power3.in, .22 s. *(set by you)*
- **ScreenZoom** (transition): A fast push (+154 % in about 5 s) into the screen of a scene, with the screen kept centred. A hard cut then shows the capture full frame. A flash variant ends on a 0.7 s white flash. — examples: [MA-29 preview](media/b96fc15968b34e8b.jpg)
- **Replay pair: normal pass + slow crop** (other): Straight cut + VHS rewind fx into REPLAY. Pass 1: the moment again at real speed with raw audio, captions and a 'REPLAY' tag. Pass 2: the same moment slowed (17-70 %, typ. 60 %) on a static crop of the subject (no push, e.g. CR [160,220,1120,760] of 1920x1080), brightened when dark (gain ~2.2 / 1.5), tags '60% SPEED' + 'BRIGHTENED' or 'ENHANCED' only when true. Optional pointers on pass 2: red circle r 110-150 px, red arrow along an arm, or a thin red line along the object (e.g. a taut chain) that ends at the event. Crop must exclude creator overlays. *(set by you)*
- **Chained map pins** (map): OSM tiles z6-z12. map1: push to pin A, place label in caps under the pin (~5-7 s). map2: both pins (A now a white dot), red trim-path line A->B draws 0.8-3.3 s, then a distance label (e.g. '~25 MI OF BEACH'). map3: push to B with a big pulse. Consecutive maps crossfade (map1 out = map2 in). Pin on the real OSM label; check on a still. *(set by you)*
- **Black hold (freeze gain 0)** (transition): A freeze frame with gain 0 = pure black under the VO, 1-6.6 s, dip in and out; or a freeze that fades its highlight then holds 1 s black. *(set by you)*
- **AUDIO ENHANCED label** (text-card): Label 'AUDIO ENHANCED' (mono tag, kind label) for the whole raw; the raw audio block is raised +3 dB in the mix. Captions only on clear fragments, else '[unclear]' / '[shouting - unclear]' on loud 2 s RMS bins (> -36 dB). Never subtitle guessed words. *(set by you)*
- **Red highlight box on object** (other): Thin red box (corner bracket draws in ~0.6 s before) around the object, smudge or light (e.g. two lights, cable ties, prints on a fuel flap), held 4-7 s, tracking the raw's push. Position measured on a full-res still. If the source zooms or moves, put the box on a freeze instead. *(set by you)*
- **End fade to black + 3 s black** (transition): Last section with no outro teaser: picture and sound fade to black over 1.5 s, then 3 s of black (FADE_OUT 1.5, END_HOLD 3). *(set by you)*
- **Teaser hard cut end** (transition): A section ends on the next case's raw teaser (~6 s, audio pre-roll ~1 s, no captions or '[shouting - unclear]' only) and hard-cuts out (FADE_OUT 0.001); the next section opens on its own card or raw. *(set by you)*
- **Channel page with name box** (page-3d): Captured real channel page (channel.png) on the 3D tilt-and-pan plane, centred, slightly zoomed in, ~4.6 s, dip or cut in; a red box draws on the channel name (box from the capture, e.g. 606,278 to 846,328) and a stamp 'CHANNEL - PLACE - DATE' runs on the shot where the VO names the creator. *(set by you)*
- **YT-dark thread panel** (comments): Recreated YouTube-dark comment panel, centred over a blurred freeze: avatar, handle, real time text and likes; creator pill on the creator's handle; red key-line highlight on the line that matters. Threads stack parent then reply; long pinned comments reveal line by line. Two panels in a row: panel 1 out = panel 2 in at the footage crossfade. *(set by you)*
- **PIP opening + VHS search** (ui-typing): The source's opening seconds in a centred picture-in-picture (62 % size, thin border) over blurred-dark copies of the same frames, tag 'VIDEO OPENING', muted; then a VHS search: ~30 stills spaced to the replay point, each held ~5 frames, racing timecode and '>> SEARCH', into the REPLAY. *(set by you)*

## Open learnings

(none)
